articles.title: The ‘maleta boys’ keep coming. Now, they’re implicating Sara Duterte
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte’s spokesperson Paolo Panelo dismisses the allegations made by another supposed bagman, calling him a 'planted witness'

blocks.text: 'CHRIS'. An alleged bagman named Chris claims to have delivered suitcases of cash to Vice President Sara Duterte. Her spokesman denies it.
Vice President Sara Duterte’s spokesperson Paolo Panelo dismisses the allegations made by another supposed bagman, calling him a 'planted witness'

items: A man named Chris, claiming to be a former driver of a Duterte ally, testified about delivering suitcases of cash to Vice President Sara Duterte.
Chris provided screenshots as evidence of his claims, stating he was instructed not to document their activities but did so anyway.
The Duterte camp dismissed Chris' allegations as fabricated.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
Another alleged bagman who claims to have delivered suitcases of cash to Vice President Sara Duterte has come forward.
On Thursday, October 29, a man using the alias “Chris” showed up at the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) to testify about the alleged deliveries.
He identified himself as the former driver of former House speaker Lord Allan Velasco, a known Duterte ally. Chris said he worked for Velasco for two years, from 2020 to 2022.
He was wearing a butter-yellow hoodie. His face was covered by a neck gaiter, leaving only his eyes visible.
Chris claimed that, from 2021 to 2022, he delivered suitcases that, he was told, contained money for Duterte, following Velasco’s instructions.
Chris said he learned that the deliveries were intended for Duterte from a certain Victor Sioco, whom he identified as Velasco’s head driver.
Chris also said he worked alongside Rodulfo Gracioso Jr., a self-confessed bagman who previously claimed to have delivered money to Duterte.
Chris, however, admitted that he never personally saw what was inside the suitcases.
Asked by reporters to back up his claims with evidence, Chris showed screenshots of his Facebook MyDay posts.
One showed a black background with the words “OTW DAVAO” in white text. Chris said he posted it on June 16, 2021. He also showed a photo of a white car that, he claimed, was driven by Sioco.
Chris said they were told not to take photos or post anything about their activities on social media. However, he said he still did, defying the instruction.

blocks.caption: ALLEGED BAGMAN. Alias ‘Chris’ shows reporters a screenshot of his Facebook MyDay post, which reads ‘OTW DAVAO,’ on October 29, 2026. He presented it as among the evidence supporting his claim that he delivered cash to Vice President Sara Duterte. Photo by Patrick Cruz/Rappler

blocks.text: Chris said one delivery took three days, with the group traveling from Manila to Matnog Port in Sorsogon before reaching Davao City.
He described their destination as a compound surrounded by tall walls and a gate.
In a written testimony submitted to the NBI, Chris recalled another alleged delivery in 2021.
He said he was driving a Toyota Hi-Ace Grandia van carrying 12 suitcases. Two bodyguards accompanied him. One of them he identified only by the nickname “Panther.”

“Nagtaka ako noon kung bakit kami may dalang ganoong karaming maleta gayong ang aming pupuntahan ay isang golf course. Napansin ko rin na may mga maleta ring karga ang sasakyan ni Boss Allan. Sinabihan ako na huwag magtanong at magkwekwento sa kung ano man ang aking nakita o narinig,” Chris said in his written statement.

(I wondered why we were bringing so many suitcases when we were only going to a golf course. I also noticed that Boss Allan’s vehicle had several suitcases in it. I was told not to ask questions or tell anyone about anything I had seen or heard.)
Upon reaching Valley Golf, Chris said the two bodyguards got out of the vehicle and brought down the suitcases while he stayed inside the car. The bodyguards returned without the luggage.
The group then headed back to Valle Verde, where Velasco lives. After the alleged delivery, Chris said Sioco handed him an envelope containing P150,000.
The Duterte camp dismissed Chris’ claims. “Another day, another tanim (planted) witness,” Duterte’s spokesperson Paolo Panelo said on Friday, October 30.
“They can keep manufacturing allegations, but they cannot fabricate the truth. As before, VP Sara will happily dismantle each allegation with evidence at the proper time,” Panelo said.
He challenged the media to “independently test and verify these claims.”
Panelo said the media, which he referred to as the “fourth estate,” were being “weaponized for the relentless, but ultimately ineffective, black propaganda against the Vice President.”
Chris is not the first person to come forward with claims about suitcases of money allegedly delivered to politicians.
Last year, in the wake of the flood control corruption scandal, several individuals identifying themselves as former drivers, bagmen, and security aides of politicians have made similar allegations.
Remember Orly Guteza, who identified himself as a bagman of former congressman Zaldy Co?

blocks.caption: The ‘maleta boys’ keep coming. Now, they’re implicating Sara Duterte

blocks.text: He claimed that he delivered money to former House speaker Martin Romualdez, but later withdrew his allegations.
Then there were Guteza’s supposed colleagues, the 18 alleged former Marines who identified themselves as former security aides of Co.
They went public with a series of claims implicating several politicians — including President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. They were accused of receiving suitcases filled with cash.
Now, there’s Chris and Gracioso, who said they were among those tasked to bring suitcases to Duterte.
From Co to Romualdez to Marcos and now Duterte, the alleged maleta (luggage) boys have been naming some of the country’s most powerful politicians.
But their accounts have also come under close scrutiny. Some claims have been denied. Others have been questioned because of inconsistencies.
So, who’s telling the truth and what are their motivations?
Are these maleta boys really coming forward to expose corruption or are they being used as pawns by warring politicians? – Rappler.com

articles.title: Friday briefing: Israel has a dilemma - can its opposition govern with Palestinian parties?
articles.summary: In today’s newsletter: Benjamin Netanyahu has been left without a majority, now it is up to the coalition to find out whether the desire for change will prove to be a defining political…

blocks.text: Good morning. It was described by many Israelis as the most consequential election in their country’s history. And, as the final votes were tallied, it has delivered a result that presents Israel with a significant dilemma.

Benjamin Netanyahu’s far-right coalition has lost its mandate while the opposition has a clear majority: but only if the Jewish Israeli opposition bloc, led by retired general Gadi Eisenkot, is prepared to make a governing pact with Palestinian Israeli parties, which have secured a historic result.

But the country that is desperate for change remains bitterly divided. After a campaign mired in racism, during which Israel’s far-right demonised the Palestinian population as the enemy within, Netanyahu has gone further since Tuesday’s vote, claiming that Palestinian-led parties have “stolen the election”, despite Israeli authorities insisting there is no evidence of election fraud.
As coalition talks commence, I spoke to our chief Middle East correspondent Emma Graham-Harrison in Tel Aviv, about false narratives and the stark choice facing the country. But first, the headlines.
Five big stories

items: UK politics | John Healey has backed away from cutting the cost of welfare this parliament, amid dire warnings his first budget could lead to brutal spending cuts because of a £28bn shortfall in public finances.

Patrick Stewart | The acclaimed British stage and screen actor renowned for both Shakespeare and sci-fi, died at his home in Los Angeles after “a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia”, his longtime spokesperson said.
Environment | One of the most ambitious nature recovery projects ever undertaken in England can go ahead after campaigners announced they had raised £30m to buy an estate in Northumberland.

Europe | Spain began three days of mourning on Thursday for at least 69 people who died in a high-speed rail collision, as hospitals continued to treat dozens of injured passengers and train drivers went on strike to urge more investment in railway safety.

US news | The Trump administration has opened a criminal investigation in California over claims that thousands of noncitizens are registered to vote in the state, and has begun subpoenaing election officials.

blocks.text: In depth: There is no evidence of election fraud

blocks.caption: Mansour Abbas, leader of the Ra’am party, is committed to working with Jewish Israeli opposition parties. Photograph: Mahmoud Illean/AP

blocks.text: With the final results released early on Friday local time, Netanyahu’s bloc won 53 seats, compared with 48 for the grouping led by rival Eisenkot. Palestinian parties won 19 seats, a record high. No single party has ever claimed a majority of 61 seats, so Israel has always been governed by coalitions.

With neither bloc reaching the 61 seats needed for a majority in the Knesset, Israeli president Isaac Herzog is expected to invite the party most likely to be able to form a government to start coalition negotiations, and has already urged politicians to have an “open mind” before talks begin. The country potentially faces weeks of rancour and uncertainty.

Yair Golan, the leader of the centre-left Democrats, a junior partner in the Jewish Israeli opposition bloc, told Israeli media on Thursday that he was meeting Eisenkot and others for initial talks. If the opposition can’t agree some kind of coalition, or even secure Palestinian support for a minority government, Netanyahu may have a lifeline. He is already pushing for a right-wing governing coalition, and would probably welcome new elections or a lengthy period of uncertainty during which he will stay on as caretaker prime minister.
And yet throughout the campaign, voters’ discontent with Netanyahu was evident.

That didn’t mean a shift to the left: young Israelis are more rightwing than older generations, as Emma wrote about here. The national conversation ahead of the election was dominated by security at home and abroad. Although he was in charge on 7 October 2023, when Hamas attacks resulted in the deaths of about 1,200 people, the majority of them civilians, the prime minister tried to shift blame on to the security services.

His opponents pledged a state commission of inquiry into the events of 7 October, and spoke to voters’ concerns about the social toll of three years of multi-front wars, and anger about the draft exemption for ultra-orthodox young men when other Israelis are spending hundreds of days on reserve duty.
Netanyahu’s false narrative

Throughout the campaign, Netanyahu and his far-right allies have framed Palestinian voters – who make up about 20% of the population – as a direct threat to ​the state, with Netanyahu repeating the slogan “the right or Palestine”, which rhymes in Hebrew.
“It’s both tragic and depressing,” Emma tells me, “attempting to paint Palestinians as untrustworthy citizens with dual loyalties, a racist trope that also appears in antisemitic attacks.”

This tactic extended to election day, when voters received a robocall purporting to come from the prime minister falsely claiming that Palestinian party leaders had been caught with envelopes full of cash. Netanyahu and his allies repeatedly made claims about high turnout in Palestinian areas, in a bid to get his own voters out.

Then on Wednesday night, Netanyahu reacted to the high Palestinian turnout and success of Arab Israeli parties by claiming, again without providing evidence, they had “stolen the election,” calling for the central elections committee and Shin Bet internal security agency to investigate foreign interference in the vote. These claims were amplified by far-right Israeli finance minister, Bezalel Smotrich, who called for the arrest of Arab Israeli leaders.

He was swiftly accused of using smear tactics to cling to power. Eisenkot warned that Likud and Netanyahu “have embarked on a coordinated, organised campaign seeking to delegitimise the results of the election”. President Herzog stepped in with a rebuke to the prime minister and said “we must avoid tarnishing an entire community”. Meanwhile, Qatar’s foreign ministry spokesperson rejected “ridiculous and dangerous” accusations his country had interfered in Tuesday’s election.
It bears repeating: Israeli police and the central elections committee have said there is no evidence of election fraud.
The Palestinian-led parties who could be kingmakers
There was a surge in support for Arab parties after Palestinian citizens came out in historic numbers to vote.

Many had boycotted previous elections “on the grounds that participating endorses a discriminatory system or because they felt their representatives had little leverage”, Emma explains. But this year, the mood changed: “They’re watching ethnic cleansing in the West Bank, a genocidal war in Gaza, and are under huge pressure inside Israel from an openly racist government, which has allowed organised crime to soar, ramped up home demolitions, and targeted political speech. They felt that, if Netanyahu managed to get another mandate with his far right allies including [extremist security minister] Ben-Gvir, this would only accelerate.”

The Joint List – which represents a number of mainly leftist Israeli Arab-led parties – is led by Yousef Jabareen. He has previously said the Joint ​List could not join an Eisenkot-led government because of its support for Israel’s ‌military operation in Gaza and southern Lebanon, but has left open the possibility of bolstering a minority government through confidence votes.

The other main Palestinian party, Ra’am, is led by Mansour Abbas, and includes a Jewish former chief of police as number two on their slate, a signal of their commitment to working with Jewish Israelis but also their desire to tackle organised crime, which is a big issue for the Palestinian population.

Ra’am joined Naftali Bennett’s government in 2021, the first time a Palestinian party entered an Israeli coalition, but their pact collapsed after 18 months, partly because of disagreements over the occupied West Bank.
The big dilemma
A survey taken as polls closed on Tuesday showed that a clear majority of opposition voters supported forming a government with Ra’am in order to unseat Netanyahu.

While Eisenkot has not ruled out cooperating with Palestinians because of their race, he has effectively barred them from a future coalition by laying out conditions for any partner which are politically impossible for them to accept.

Still, Emma notes an inconsistency: Palestinian citizens play a key role in Israeli life, with outsized representation in professions from medics to security guards, including much of the team at Eisenkot’s election night HQ. “You would think some of these parties might ask, if you trust Palestinian citizens to secure your campaign events why don’t you trust them to be part of your government?”

Emma points to a rarely referenced precedent from three decades ago, when Yitzhak Rabin relied on Palestinian support for a minority government as he sought a negotiated end to the Israel-Palestine conflict. Might such a compromise be possible now?

“This whole campaign has been based on Israeli voters urgently wanting change, because Netanyahu has led them to the brink of disaster. And now they have voted, this is an existential moment,” she said

“You have a parliamentary majority to bring about that change. Is your racism ultimately more important to you? What matters more: the desire to exclude Palestinians or the desire to get rid of Netanyahu?”

A bit of good news to remind you that the world’s not all bad

blocks.caption: An electric ferry in New York. Photograph: Climate Central

blocks.text: Moving away from diesel-powered ferries to electric vessels has not been an easy task. Batteries are heavy, which means more power is needed to propel electric boats forward through significant resistance. But more companies are finding solutions to the problem and creating workable vessels that reduce emissions.

One such company is Vessev, whose electric ferries rely on underwater wings called hydrofoils that lift the boat above the water. This dramatically reduces drag by up to 66%, making their boats more energy-efficient. Swedish company Candela are designing boats, they claim, which can reduce energy use by 80% compared with conventional vessels of a similar type. “I think in a more sustainable future we’re likely to see more and more vessels like this around the world,” Eric Laakmann, the chief executive and co-founder of Vessev, said.

articles.title: NAPOLCOM probes Samar cop who allegedly kicked pregnant partner, causing miscarriage
articles.summary: The National Police Commission (NAPOLCOM) on Friday said it is investigating allegations of physical abuse against a police officer after his former live-in partner filed a complaint.

blocks.text: The National Police Commission (NAPOLCOM) on Friday said it is investigating allegations of physical abuse against a police officer after his former live-in partner filed a complaint.
According to the complainant, the police officer identified as Police Corporal Rogen Cain repeatedly assaulted her even when she was pregnant.
“Way back 2021, January po ako po ay nakunan. Namatay po yung baby ko. Which is sa summer pa lang po, wala na po palang heartbeat yung baby ko,” the complainant said at a press conference.
(Way back in January 2021, I had a miscarriage. My baby died. I did not know that my baby had no heartbeat since summer.)
“Alam po 'yan ng pulis na nirereklamo ko. Nawala po yung anak ko dahil po sa pananakit po niya sa akin,” she added.
(The police I complained about know that. My child is gone because he hurt me.)
The complainant, whose identity was withheld due to the sensitive nature of the case, appeared before NAPOLCOM and sought assistance in investigating the officer.
She alleged that Cain kicked her in the back while she was pregnant, resulting in the miscarriage of their first child.
According to her, the cop also physically assaulted her during another argument while she was pregnant with their second child, causing her to bleed and nearly lose the baby.

She also further recounted an incident in which they struggled over a tactical pen knife, leaving both of them injured, and another confrontation in which the officer allegedly pointed a firearm at her and accidentally fired it, hitting a wall.
'Dismissed'
Also present during the presser, Cain said the issues had already been addressed in previous proceedings, claiming that the criminal cases filed against him had been dismissed.

“Na-serve ko na yun lahat yung allegations niya. Simula yung sa criminal case, yung finile niya doon sa Calbayog, na-provisional dismissed na po ‘yun. Tapos yung sinabi niya na nakunan siya, nag-file siya ng kaso dyan doon sa Lower Bicutan, Taguig, na dismissed na din yan,” he said.

(I have served all of her allegations. Starting with the criminal case, the one she filed in Calbayog, it has been provisionally dismissed. Then when she said he had a miscarriage, she filed a case in Lower Bicutan, Taguig, which has also been dismissed.)
According to him, the Philippine National Police - Internal Affairs Service (PNP-IAS) had imposed a 60-day suspension on him over a physical injuries complaint.
However, Cain denied stabbing the complainant with a tactical pen knife and firing a gun.
“Hindi yun. Siya lang ang nanaksak sa akin. Pagdaan ko noon, bigla niya akong sinaksak. May medical ako…Wala po akong idea nyan [na nagpaputok ako],” the police officer said.
(That's not true. She was the one who stabbed me. When I was passing by, she suddenly stabbed me. I have a medical record…I have no idea about the firing incident.)
The complaint said that she had reported the matter to PNP-IAS but she was disappointed that the cop is still in the service.
“Sana ma-imbestigahan po yung IAS po ng PNP at saka yung kaso po na finile ko po sa kanya. Kasi, sa totoo lang po, alam ko po na may merong mga taong tumulong sa kanya regarding po dyan,” she said.
(I hope the IAS of the PNP and the case I filed against him will be investigated. Because, to be honest, I know that there are people who helped him regarding that.)
“Napaka-unfair po ng IAS po ng PNP na hanggang ngayon yung taong yun is aktibo sa serbisyo,” she added.
(PNP-IAS is so unfair that until now that person is still active in the service.)
NAPOLCOM Commissioner Ralph Calinisan said the Commission would coordinate with the IAS to determine the status and outcome of the previous complaint.
GMA News Online has sought comment from PNP-IAS about the matter but it has yet to provide a statement as of posting time.

“Hindi tayo papayag na isang abusadong pulis ay nagtatagal sa serbisyo. Uulitin ko, tiwala ng tao ang pinag-uusapan dito. Kaya nga siya lumapit sa atin para aksyunan natin yung kanilang problema. Kaya pangangalagaan natin yung tiwala ng tao sa paglapit sa atin,” he said.

(We will not allow an abusive police officer to remain in service for long. I repeat, what is at stake here is the trust of the people. That is why they came to us so that we can take action on their concerns. That is why we will protect the trust of the people.) —VAL, GMA News

articles.summary: Macacua's election marks the transition from an appointed interim authority to a regular regional government following parliametary elections on September 14

blocks.text: BARMM CHIEF. Former acting Maguindanao del Norte governor Abdulraof 'Sammy Gambar' Macacua is appointed the interim chief minister of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao in March 2025.
Abdulraof "Sammy Gambar" Macacua Facebook
Macacua's election marks the transition from an appointed interim authority to a regular regional government following parliametary elections on September 14

items: Abdulraof 'Sammy Gambar' Macacua was elected chief minister of the Bangsamoro region on October 30, ending seven years of transition governance.
Macacua secured a majority vote in the 80-member Bangsamoro Parliament, defeating former interim chief minister Ahod 'Al Haj Murad' Ebrahim.
His election signifies the transition to a regular regional government following parliamentary elections and the dissolution of the unelected Bangsamoro Transition Authority.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

COTABATO, Philippines – Abdulraof “Sammy Gambar” Macacua was elected chief minister of the Bangsamoro region on Friday, October 30, securing a majority vote in the newly constituted parliament and ending seven years of transition governance.

Macacua won 51 votes in the 80-member Bangsamoro Parliament, defeating former interim chief minister Ahod “Al Haj Murad” Ebrahim, chairman of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) and the United Bangsamoro Justice Party.
Ebrahim got 27 votes, one member of parliament abstained, and another was absent during Friday’s session.
Macacua’s election marks the transition from an appointed interim authority to a regular regional government following parliamentary elections on September 14.

Macacua, who represents the 3rd parliamentary district of Maguindanao del Norte under the Bangsamoro Federalist Party (BFP), previously served as interim chief minister and before that, acting provincial governor. He had also served as a senior minister of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM).
He was a prominent MILF leader and chief of staff of its armed wing, the Bangsamoro Islamic Armed Forces.

Macacua was formerly a leading member of the United Bangsamoro Justice Party, the political arm of the MILF, but later broke with its leadership after he was appointed interim chief minister, replacing Ebrahim.
He subsequently led the months-old Bangsamoro Federalist Party.
Ebrahim or Murad led the Bangsamoro transition government when the autonomous region was established in 2019 until President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. replaced him as interim chief minister.

Friday’s election followed the dissolution of the unelected Bangsamoro Transition Authority (BTA), which had overseen the region’s legislative groundwork and the passage of key codes on education, local governance and elections.
The transition stems from the ratification of the Bangsamoro Organic Law, which established the autonomous region under a peace agreement between the government and the MILF.

The 80 regular members of parliament, representing geographic districts, political parties and marginalized sectors, formally assumed their legislative and executive responsibilities from the interim BTA.
Under the region’s parliamentary system, a member of parliament can be nominated for chief minister and must secure an absolute majority of the 80-member chamber.
The inauguration was attended by national government officials, provincial governors, mayors, district representatives, peace advocates, international observers and foreign diplomats.
Macacua is expected to assemble his Cabinet, including deputy chief ministers whose appointments require parliamentary approval.
Authorities enforced heightened security in Cotabato City ahead of the inaugural session. The police and military deployed troops to strategic locations and entry points to ensure peace and order.
The heightened security, however, disrupted local businesses and drew criticism from vendors and residents concerned about restricted movement and lost income. – Rappler.com

articles.title: House insertions for farm-to-market roads came from DA list – spox
articles.summary: The agriculture department says copy-paste errors caused faulty farm-to-market road coordinates

blocks.text: PATCHWORK. Vegetable gardens on Cordillera, as seen from the Kiangan-Tinoc-Buguias road.
Angie de Silva/Rappler
The agriculture department says copy-paste errors caused faulty farm-to-market road coordinates

items: House lawmakers' insertions for farm-to-market roads are based on a validated master list from the Department of Agriculture.
Errors in coordinates for some projects were attributed to human error during the copy-pasting process, leading to significant discrepancies.
The People's Budget Coalition plans to collaborate with the Department of Agriculture to correct the flagged coordinates and improve support for agricultural infrastructure.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – House lawmakers’ insertions for farm-to-market roads (FMRs) are not made up but come from a validated master list by the Department of Agriculture (DA), the agency’s spokesman told reporters on Thursday, October 29.

DA spokesman Arnel de Mesa said lawmakers could have taken projects from the DA’s early budget proposals submitted to the Department of Budget and Management (DBM), or from the master list of the farm-to-market network plan.
“‘Yung kinukuha naman ng Congress, galing din ‘yun doon sa listahan namin,” said De Mesa. (The projects Congress inserts, those came from our own list.)

“Kaya lang kapag kino-kopya nga nila ng mga tao nila o sinasalin, nagkakaroon ng problema sa coordinates,” he added. (Although sometimes when their staff copies or transfers these projects, they make mistakes with the coordinates.)

The People’s Budget Coalition (PBC) flagged hundreds of insertions in the House of Representatives’ version of the 2027 proposed budget. These insertions, said the PBC, lack publicly available supporting documents.

The PBC also flagged coordinates for some farm-to-market roads that, when plotted, ended up at sea. De Mesa said DA officials recently met with the PBC and explained that the errors resulted from “human error” in copying and pasting coordinates.
Missing digits in coordinates could result in discrepancies of at least 100 kilometers.
“Hindi maiwasan yung human error doon sa pag-copy-paste. Actually tama ‘yung project, ‘yung pagkaka-copy lang noong coordinates talaga,” he said.
(Human error in copy-pasting is unavoidable. The projects are correct, there were just mistakes in copying the coordinates.)
Meanwhile, Kenneth Isaiah Abanta, co-founder of PBC, said the meeting with DA was “a breath of fresh air.”

“We will work together with DA to correct the coordinates of farm-to-market roads we flagged that were inserted by the House, and submit findings to Senator Kiko Pangilinan’s committee,” Abante said in a post.
Abante also called for better support for the DA’s Bureau of Agricultural and Fisheries Engineering (BAFE), the agency’s arm dealing with agriculture infrastructure. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Dizon fumes at airport officials for not handing CCTV control to NNIC
articles.summary: Transportation Secretary Vince Dizon on Friday scolded Manila International Airport Authority (MIAA) officials for failing to pass control over CCTV cameras to the new private management of the Ninoy…

blocks.text: Published October 30, 2026 2:14pm

Transportation Secretary Vince Dizon on Friday scolded Manila International Airport Authority (MIAA) officials for failing to pass control over CCTV cameras to the new private management of the Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA).
In a video report by GMA News' Gabriel Gonzales, Dizon could be seen fuming at MIAA officials for the delay in the transfer.
"Mahigit isang taon na 'yun eh… ang problema dito, walang single accountability," Dizon said. (It has been more than one year. The problem here is there is no single accountability.)

An airport official could be seen explaining to Dizon that they were waiting for the end of a contract before it transferred control of the CCTVs to the New NAIA Infra Corp. (NNIC). However, Dizon said it has been too long.
The argument stemmed from a theft incident that occurred in the airport, but the security footage could not be seen.

"Simpleng-simple 'yung problema natin. May nanakawan, hindi natin makita-kita sa CCTV. Tapos kayong lahat… nagtuturuan kayong lahat. Kaya ako nabibuwisit sa inyo," Dizon said, who later cursed as he vented his anger.
(Our problem is very simple. There was a theft, and we could not see it in the CCTV. And all of you… you are pointing at one another. That is why I am so angry with all of you.)
In a separate video report from Gabriel Gonzales, Dizon explained that he was angry that it has been one year and a half since he ordered that control over the CCTVs be handed over to the NNIC.
"Binigyan ko sila ngayong November. 'Pag hindi pa nila nalipat 'yan sesante 'yung mga ito," Dizon said. (I gave them until November. If they do not transfer it, these people are fired.)
During his visit to the NAIA, Dizon also went to the area where the incident occurred. The Transportation secretary said footage has been found of the actual incident.
"I'm very, very happy to report na nahuli na at naibalik na, o na-recover na 'yung mga nanakaw. And according to the law enforcement natin dito, kumpleto 'yung mga nanakaw na items," Dizon said.

(I'm very, very happy to report that the thief has been caught and it has been returned, or the stolen items have been returned. And according to law enforcement officers here, the items stolen are complete.)
Dizon recently reassumed control of the Department of Transportation (DOTr) after switching Cabinet posts with now Public Works and Highways Secretary Giovanni Lopez. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Syrians struggle with soaring prices as crisis challenges post-Assad recovery
articles.summary: Fuel price rises are driving discontent, testing support for Ahmed al-Sharaa's government.

blocks.text: Last month, protests erupted in squares and streets across Syria. People burned tyres, blocked roads and chanted slogans, angry at the government's decision to raise fuel prices again. It was the largest show of discontent yet since President Ahmed al-Sharaa came to power two years ago.

Speaking on a Syrian TV channel, a man said he still supported the authorities but that his situation had deteriorated to the point where he could no longer afford to buy bread. "Honestly," another said, "we have begun to fear what kind of new decision each morning will bring".

The increase was the latest in a series of measures people blame for a growing cost-of-living crisis. For many Syrians, life, financially, has worsened since rebels led by Sharaa ousted President Bashar al-Assad, ending five decades of his family's brutal rule and more than 13 years of a devastating civil war.
Catapulted to the presidency, Sharaa has, since then, led Syria's transition and efforts to revive a broken economy after a long period of mismanagement, isolation and conflict.

There was never any doubt about how challenging this would be. But as they celebrated Assad's overthrow and their new freedoms, Syrians, perhaps unrealistically, hoped things would quickly improve. That, however, has not materialised, and the handling of the economy has frustrated many here.
From essential bills to basic items, the cost of virtually everything has gone up. And many saw a further and unexpected rise in fuel prices as a sign of a government out of touch with its country.
"We don't want roundabouts. Every day they build a new roundabout. People stood by you and are still with you," another protester said, addressing Sharaa, "but this will [make] things explode".
Days later, amid calls for further demonstrations, the increase was revoked.
In a suburb of Damascus, I joined Fatima Saleh Eid at an open-air market for her weekly shop. At 50, she works as a cleaner to help support her family.

"We've suffered a lot," she said. Her husband had recently been hired by a ceramic factory after a year unemployed. He is among the lucky ones, as many are struggling to find work. In some streets, men gather in the hope of meeting someone offering a day job; often, they wait in vain.

Since coming to power, the government has slashed long-held subsidies as part of an austerity drive. The price of bread, a Syrian staple, has increased tenfold. Fuel prices are now in line with the international average, which has put pressure on farmers and made transportation more expensive, while the cost of electricity has gone up several hundred per cent for some.
The authorities, in response, have adjusted public sector wages, including pensions; unsurprisingly, the effect of the additional pay for people has been lost as prices keep rising.
"We eat more sparingly now. We can't afford chicken anymore nor meat. We only eat vegetables but even [that is] expensive," Fatima said. "Inshallah [God willing] things will get cheaper."

As she spoke, around a dozen people, of all ages, gathered around us. Nobody disagreed. One elderly man also said he had stopped eating meat. Another, in his 20s, told me his family were no longer able to pay the medicine for his father, who had a heart condition. One young woman said she and her four children could only afford to have a proper meal every two days.
Marwan Bashour, a 68-year-old pensioner, said his monthly pay was around $90 (£70), which is the public sector minimum wage. "It's not enough at all," he said.
The United Nations Development Programme said 90% of Syrians were in poverty last year.
Marwan told me how he made ends meet.
"Sometimes I borrow money, sometimes I sell things from my house," he said, "like an old pot or plates that we never used, gifts that were given to us. I've even had to sell furniture".

There have been other pressures too. Like many Syrians, Marwan used to rely on help from aid agencies. But, for him, that has stopped, as organisations have been forced to cut back services because of funding cuts.
Sharaa has, of course, scored some important gains.
International sanctions imposed in the Assad-era have been lifted, and the US has removed the country from its list of state sponsors of terrorism.
Security remains volatile and a source of concern, but the country feels more stable.

And the president continues to consolidate his power and, earlier this year, retook the resource-rich north-east from a Kurdish-led militia. (The Druze still control areas in the south, where they want to create an autonomous state; Israel occupies parts of the south-west.)
But real economic recovery is yet to happen. Large parts of Syria remain in ruins after a war that killed half a million people and displaced half of the population.

Unable to afford rent, many families live in partially destroyed buildings. The World Bank says reconstruction costs are estimated at $216bn and, without foreign help and investment, it will be impossible for Syrians to rebuild.

Samir Aita, a Syrian economist who heads the Circle of Arab Economists, a Paris-based independent think-tank, said the crisis was a "combination of policies with the [government] not managing expectations and creating unrealistic hopes".
When I asked him about how he felt about the future, he said: "It's unsustainable. If they don't change, I fear chaos."
Exhausted after years of conflict, Syrians, left with almost no choice, remain hopeful.
Abu Mahmoud, a cab driver, told me: "They inherited the country bankrupt, so people need to be patient. Things don't happen overnight."
Additional reporting by Lana Antaki, Samantha Granville and Neha Sharma

articles.title: UK government’s obesity plan ‘doomed to fail’, MPs warn
articles.summary:
Cross-party committee says ‘moonshot’ vow to end obesity epidemic in a decade will fail without personal leadership from PM

The UK government’s promise to reverse rising obesity rates in the…

blocks.text: The UK government’s promise to reverse rising obesity rates in the next decade is “doomed to fail” without a major rethink and a new plan led directly by the prime minister, a cross-party committee of MPs has concluded.

The health and social care select committee said in a report that there are no signs the so-called “moonshot ambition on obesity”, set out in the 10-year health plan for England, will achieve anything significant.

More than a year after the promise to “end the obesity epidemic” within a decade was made, even the most basic questions – such as how progress will be measured and how a cross-departmental plan would work – remain unanswered, the MPs said.

The report said: “While the ambition to ‘end the obesity epidemic’ is a laudable one, we currently have no faith in the government’s commitment to this aim or ability to achieve it and predict that, unless they urgently reassess their approach, they are doomed to fail.
“The government will fail to tackle a challenge of this scale unless action is led from the top and delivery of the moonshot is made a clear, personal priority of the prime minister.”
It called for the creation of a dedicated cabinet committee on the obesity plan, chaired by the prime minister, to drive action and “to send a message that this government takes obesity seriously”.

According to the most recent official statistics, 30% of adults in England are living with obesity, with 66% either overweight or living with obesity. Close to a third of children are now estimated to be overweight or living with obesity. Obesity rates for adults and children have increased significantly since the 1990s and, while the trends have levelled off, there are no signs of a fall.

One of the major failings of the current strategy, the report said, is a lack of proper distinction between efforts to prevent future obesity, for example by cracking down on unhealthy foods, and those to support and treat people who already have obesity.
“Conflating these two things is in part responsible for the muddled thinking and lack of progress from successive governments to date,” the MPs said.

Any effective plan must be based on a clear definition of what the ambition to reduce obesity rates means in practical terms, along with interim progress markers that would allow MPs to hold ministers to account, they said.

The MPs also called for a “joined-up, cross-government action plan”, taking in the departments responsible, their planned actions and how these will be funded, covering prevention and treatment for adults and children.
Ministers should come to parliament within the next three months to set out the plan, the report said.

Leadership from No 10 was vital, said Layla Moran, the Liberal Democrat MP who chairs the committee. She added an effective plan “will mean standing up to the food industry on numerous points – regulating the constant presence of adverts and promotions for unhealthy food and drink that wallpaper our lives, simpler labelling on products, targets for supermarkets to sell more healthy foods and restricting fast food outside schools”.

She said: “This issue transcends government departments, and experience tells us that if the prime minister isn’t calling the shots on such a huge societal issue, the loose ends won’t join up and the moonshot will crash land.
“We urge him to take up this ambition and be the driver of change. In turn, the NHS, public health and the economy will reap the long-term benefits.”

A Department of Health and Social Care spokesperson said: “Obesity is one of the biggest challenges facing our health service, and this government is taking bold action to help drive the shift from sickness to prevention and give every child the best start in life.

“We have already restricted junk food advertising on television before 9pm and online, banned volume-price promotions on less healthy food and drink products, and given councils stronger powers to block new hot food takeaways near schools.

“Alongside our focus on prevention, we are supporting those already living with obesity by expanding access to weight management support, including NHS weight-loss drugs for those with the greatest clinical need.”

articles.title: Battle lines redrawn in Spain’s snap election after latest train disaster
articles.summary:
Next month’s poll no longer the contest it was, as Pedro Sánchez finds himself forced to defend government’s safety record

One of the most dependable cliches of contemporary Spanish politics…

blocks.text: One of the most dependable cliches of contemporary Spanish politics is that it never pays to bet against Pedro Sánchez. Time and time again – as leader of the Spanish Socialist Workers’ party (PSOE) and as prime minister – Sánchez has shown an almost preternatural ability to profit from adversity, and to confound expectations and wrongfoot his opponents.

But next month’s snap general election, called by Sánchez after rightwing and far-right parties voted down the housing reforms his coalition government had announced in response to angry protests, may suddenly not be the contest it once was.

Wednesday’s deadly rail collision, in which at least 69 people died, has, for the moment at least, subdued much of the vicious language and posturing that has come to characterise recent elections. The crash could sap Sánchez’s recently resurgent momentum and the issue of rail safety now threatens to overshadow his attempts to defend his record and remain in the Moncloa palace.

The poll the left had billed as a last chance to stop the conservative People’s party (PP) joining forces with the rightwing Vox party to roll back decades of social progress – and which the right had billed as an opportunity to end eight years of what it disdainfully calls sanchismo – will now take place in a country deep in shock and grief.

Not only has Spain’s extensive high-speed railway long been a source of national pride, it is also a transport network that millions of Spaniards depend on for work, holidays and family visits. This week’s crash, after another on the same line that killed 46 people in January, has left people angry, bewildered and worried.

blocks.caption: Emergency crews on Thursday work to remove the wreckage of two high-speed trains from the crash site in Urda, Toledo. Photograph: Burak Akbulut/Anadolu/Getty Images

blocks.text: Thursday’s headlines spoke for themselves. El Mundo’s front page lamented “Another massacre on the trains”; ABC’s noted “At least 68 dead nine months on”, while El País mourned the “Second high-speed catastrophe in less than a year.”

Even before Wednesday’s terrible events on the outskirts of Urda, Sánchez and his allies were facing a battle. As well as the housing protests, the prime minister has had to contend with a slew of corruption allegations surrounding his family and inner circle, while his government’s handling of the mass crossing into Spain’s north African territory of Ceuta over the summer had been fiercely criticised at home and abroad.

Pablo Simón, a political scientist at the Carlos III University of Madrid, stressed the delicacy of the moment, saying that people across Spain were still struggling to come to terms with what had happened this week.

“There are a lot of fronts [for the government] here, and I think this accident has a twofold impact,” he said. “First, it draws attention to the state of railway infrastructure, suggesting that the problem is structural, and pointing to a broader decline in public services in Spain, specifically regarding infrastructure.”

Simón said that Sánchez’s government, which has been in power since 2018, could not blame the state of things on its PP predecessor, which carried out austerity cuts. “That’s simply not credible,” he said.
“But there’s also a second issue: even before this, the government faced an uphill battle; it was already highly unlikely that they could secure the necessary support.”

Sánchez has said it is “unacceptable” for the country to experience two high-speed rail disasters in less than a year, and promised to strengthen safety measures “so that something like this never happens again”, but his opponents say that is simply not good enough.

The PP leader, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, said on Thursday that any politician found to be responsible for the crash would be held to account, adding: “We can’t go on like this; this kind of management just can’t carry on.” According to the PP, Spaniards are not asking for “miracles; they’re just asking for a Spain where things work again”.

blocks.caption: The PP leader, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, also visited the scene on Thursday. Photograph: Pablo Blázquez Domínguez/Getty Images

blocks.text: Vox, on the other hand, is going all out, accusing the government of “killing” the train crash victims and of systemic mismanagement and cronyism. It has also urged the supreme court to investigate Spain’s transport minister, Óscar Puente, on suspicion of manslaughter and causing bodily harm through gross negligence. Puente has rejected allegations of mismanagement, insisting that Spain’s railway system is “safe and reliable”.

Simón said the contrasting reactions of the PP and Vox reflected splits on the right, as both parties compete to put an end to Sánchez’s government: “The question becomes what tone should one adopt: a more institutional one, which is what the PP is currently attempting, or a tougher, more aggressive one, which is what Vox is doing?”

He also suggested the sombre national mood could make it very hard for Sánchez to rally as many as 1.2 million “politically dormant” but PSOE-leaning voters, on whom he had been counting. The electoral event the prime minister had hoped to portray as a Manichean clash between progressives and reactionaries, fought over issues of housing and equality, has morphed into something else.
“An election campaign relies on high spirits and a sense of optimism,” Simón said. “But how can that exist when the entire country is in mourning over this tragedy?”

articles.title: Hitting the fan: London council angers residents with removal of 700 dog-waste bins
articles.summary:
Conservative-run Hillingdon aims to save £100,000 but local people fear dog poo will ‘be dumped everywhere’

People in a west London borough fear it will become covered in dog poo after their…

blocks.text: People in a west London borough fear it will become covered in dog poo after their cash-strapped council decided to remove 700 dog-waste bins to save money.
“People are worried there’s going to be dog shit everywhere,” said Daniel O’Neill, the chief road steward at Ruislip Residents’ Association.
Hillingdon’s pet dogs produce about 174 tonnes of faeces each year, which, until now, has been generally bagged up by their owners and deposited in dog-waste bins.

The Conservative-run council believes it will save £100,000 in waste collection costs by removing the bins. It hopes dog owners will use general litter bins instead, but O’Neill and many other people are unconvinced.

“Everybody’s going to have a Christmas tree of dog-shit baubles in their front garden because there’ll be nowhere else to put the bags of it,” O’Neill said. “I got one of those AI generators to make me a Christmas tree with dog-shit bags in different colours, to show what’s going to happen.”
Sital Punja who walks Marley, her springer-poodle, every day in Ruislip woods, said the “preposterousness” of the bin removals have dominated chat between dog walkers.

“People are really unhappy about it, it’s going to be dumped everywhere,” said Punja, who is an opposition Labour councillor. “The dog bins in the woods are already overflowing and there aren’t enough general bins. The dog bins have lids so the smell stays inside. General bins don’t, so they stink and can be got at by foxes.”

blocks.caption: Overflowing, dog-waste bins in Hillingdon. Photograph: Daniel O’Neill

blocks.text: Hillingdon is not the first council to remove dog-waste bins to try to save money. Similar plans have prompted outrage in Cornwall, Kent, North Somerset and elsewhere.

Hillingdon borough’s large debts are increasing by £5.6m a year. Its schools grant deficit alone is £101.5m and the government has “serious concerns” about the borough’s finances, which could jeopardise its chances of continuing to rely on exceptional financial support grants from Whitehall.
At the same time, Hillingdon prides itself on having frozen council tax for years. This was the root of the problem, according to O’Neill, who said he had observed the last 150 council meetings.

“If they put the council taxes up, even to just the average in London, then they would bring in £26m,” he said, “but what they’re actually doing instead is not emptying the dog-shit bins to save £100,000.”

O’Neill said it was this issue that had really cut through with residents. “I tell people about the deficit, or about the audit problems, and nobody cares. When I tell them that their bins are going to get taken away, they go nuts.”
Comments on Ruislip’s residents’ association Facebook page appear to bear this out.

“What an absurd suggestion,” said one person. Another said it was “madness” and added: “Are they trying to completely alienate the residents? There are enough selfish dog owners who already don’t pick up after their dogs so they think removing the bins will improve that?”
after newsletter promotion
One resident said: “Sadly this is probably a decision by someone who does not have a clue how much shit is created by dogs. As a dog owner there are not enough bins. This is shortsighted.”

blocks.caption: ‘To have to take away dog bins; it’s desperate.’ Photograph: Daniel O’Neill

blocks.text: Punja said Hillingdon had a lot of dog owners. “During Covid the rise of dog owners was astronomical. I was one of those Covid dog owners.”

She added: “This is just one of the council’s harebrained ideas they have come up with when they can’t balance the books … It probably would be simpler to put up council tax. I can only describe it as dog-shit, excuse my language – but to have to scramble to such a level where you have to take away dog bins; it’s desperate.”
A council report setting out the plan said it would save £160,000, of which £60,000 would be reinvested in street cleaning.

Wayne Bridges, the council’s cabinet member for residents’ services, said: “We do understand that some residents have concerns about these changes. We are simply changing how it is collected, making better use of the nearly 1,500 ordinary litter bins already available across Hillingdon.

“By allowing dog waste to be placed in ordinary public litter bins, which can already be used safely for this purpose, more than doubling existing capacity, we can bring collections into our existing street cleansing arrangements and remove the cost of running two separate services.
“Many councils across the country already allow dog waste to be disposed of through general waste arrangements.”

articles.title: Security guard who protected Nigel Farage on campaign trail was facing rape charge
articles.summary:
Ryan Dinnage – who accompanied Reform UK leader on walkabouts before local elections – was later jailed, raising questions about vetting failure

One of Nigel Farage’s security team who…

blocks.text: One of Nigel Farage’s security team who accompanied him on the local election campaign trail this year was facing a rape charge and was later jailed for eight years, raising questions about a failure of vetting.
Ryan Dinnage spent time protecting Farage in April and May, but in June was convicted of having raped a woman while she slept in a caravan at the Royal Windsor horse show.

Dinnage was seen beside Farage on walkabouts on at least four occasions on Reform’s local election campaign trail this spring: in Llandudno, Conwy County; Waterlooville, Hampshire, Worthing, West Sussex, and Downham Market, Norfolk.
He had been charged in 2025, three years after the crime took place at the equestrian event in 2022.

blocks.caption: Ryan Dinnage, 32, from Croydon, was sentenced in July to more than eight years in prison. Photograph: Thames Valley police

blocks.text: Reform UK acknowledged Farage was provided with protection by Dinnage, and said his services had been supplied by a third-party contractor who had assured them he had been vetted.
A spokesperson for the party said: “As soon as we found out, we were shocked and disgusted and he ceased to be used by Reform.”

However, the episode raises questions about how a security operative facing a charge of serious sexual violence could have been put in a position of responsibility near a senior politician and members of the public.
Reform UK did not answer further questions about whether the party was continuing its relationship with the third-party contractor, and whether any action was taken against them.

A Labour spokesperson said: “Nigel Farage must urgently explain at what point Reform UK became aware that they allowed a man charged with rape to directly interact with the public on their behalf. They must also urgently make clear what action they have taken to prevent such a situation happening again.

“Farage and his party are lurching from scandal to scandal and the public are rapidly seeing who they really are. In recent weeks Farage has shrugged off vile misogyny and Reform has an appalling track record when it comes to standing up for women. It’s time Farage showed some leadership for once, got his house in order, and realised the buck stops with him.”

Farage is generally accompanied by a large security team, and has spoken of threats being made against him. The man accused of murdering Ann Widdecombe has been charged with engaging in conduct in preparation of acts of terrorism, including against Farage. Over the summer, counter-terror police reopened a year-long investigation into an alleged firebomb attack at Farage’s home in south London.

The Reform UK leader has repeatedly said he accepted a £5m gift from the crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne in order to pay for his security for the rest of his life. He has previously turned down taxpayer-funded security from the government, which included a bodyguard, a car, and a trained driver, deeming it to be inadequate.

Dinnage, then 32, of Croydon, was sentenced to eight and half years in prison in July. According to Thames Valley police, his offence took place in the early hours of 16 May 2022, when Dinnage entered the caravan where the victim was sleeping and raped her. He was reported to police later that day and arrested the next day.

Reform is not the only party in the spotlight for a vetting failure in recent weeks. The Conservatives were criticised, by Reform UK, for having employed a former election candidate, Jack Ross, who was filmed by an undercover reporter appearing to discuss the cost of hiring contract killers. Ross had worked as a consultant in Kemi Badenoch’s office.

Ross is facing an investigation by the Tories after he was filmed apparently asking an undercover reporter: “What do you want done?” and apparently offering to “broker” the services of an alleged far-right paramilitary group.

Police in Scotland have said they will be reviewing an Al Jazeera documentary in which Ross was filmed seemingly making a range of comments about what a contract killer could be employed to do, and talked about using far-right groups to create disruption on the streets.

articles.title: TUC leader expects wave of union recognition in private sector over coming year
articles.summary:
Paul Nowak says ‘hundreds, if not thousands’ of employers could sign access agreements as ‘transformative’ rules come into force

The TUC general secretary, Paul Nowak, is predicting a…

blocks.text: The TUC general secretary, Paul Nowak, is predicting a wave of union recognition deals in the private sector over the next year as “transformative” rules on accessing workplaces come into force.

From Friday, as part of Labour’s Employment Rights Act, unions will have the right to enter workplaces or communicate with staff electronically. From January, employers will be obliged to inform workers of their right to join a union.

“I think it potentially could be transformative,” Nowak said. “This could open up large parts of … the private sector, where unions have been trying to get a foothold but have been hampered partly because of the legal framework. It gives us a real opportunity.”

He added: “My prediction would be that by this time next year, we’ll have signed hundreds, if not thousands of new recognition agreements with employers, taking that union voice into the private sector in particular.”

Polling carried out for the TUC by YouGov suggests 62% of workers would support a trade union negotiating on their behalf on pay and conditions, but 36% of those who are not members of a union say they would not know how to join one.

Nowak pointed to a flurry of recent deals, citing agreements between John Lewis and Usdaw and between the GMB and the Maritime and Coastguard Agency as evidence that some employers are responding even before the rules have come into force.

“What we’re seeing is a whole range of employers, who have recognised that the legislation is changing, that the political climate is changed and are now reaching voluntary agreements with unions,” he said.

blocks.caption: Nowak pointed to recent deals, including one between John Lewis and Usdaw, as evidence employers are acting before rules apply. Photograph: Tony Buckingham/John Lewis/PA

blocks.text: Just over a fifth of the UK’s workforce are trade union members, down from more than half in 1979, before Margaret Thatcher came to power.

Under the new rules, there will be a formal process to request access to a workplace if a union cannot agree with the employer, which will be overseen by the regulator, the Central Arbitration Committee.

Previously, unions trying to win the right to represent a workforce have sometimes had to do so from outside the building – as was the case with the GMB’s thwarted effort to win recognition at Amazon’s warehouse near Coventry two years ago.
Nowak said Labour’s new approach “changes the mood, and I think it brings us much more into the European mainstream, which is that unions are part and parcel of the workplace”.

The access rights are the latest element of the government’s upgrade to workers’ rights to be implemented. Rights to sick pay have already been extended and further changes, including restrictions on zero hours contracts, are yet to come into force.
Some employers have complained about the potential costs of the new regime, but Nowak insisted good bosses need not worry.

“Genuinely, employers have got nothing to fear from this. They shouldn’t see their staff wanting an independent voice as somehow a negative verdict on them. You can work for a good, successful organisation and still want a strong, independent union voice.”

articles.title: FWC 2026 draws 7,000 on-site attendees, Astral claims three-peat win
articles.summary: The ‘Flyff Universe World Championship (FWC) 2026’ came to a close with Team Astral securing their third consecutive title. The Grand Finals, held on October 24 at the SM Mall of Asia…

blocks.text: The ‘Flyff Universe World Championship (FWC) 2026’ came to a close with Team Astral securing their third consecutive title. The Grand Finals, held on October 24 at the SM Mall of Asia Music Hall in Manila, Philippines, drew 7,000 on-site attendees, while cumulative streaming viewers reached 50,000.

FWC is the global esports tournament for ‘Flyff Universe,’ an HTML5 MMORPG developed by Gala Lab and published by Wemade Connect. Originally launched as an online tournament in 2023, the event marked its fourth edition this year. In these finals, eight teams composed of players from seven countries—including the Philippines, the United States, France, and Chile—competed for a total prize pool of $110,000 (approx. 146 million won).

This year’s journey began on April 23 on dedicated FWC servers. Participants leveled up new characters from Level 1, preparing equipment and strategies before earning their spots on the Manila stage through qualifiers. The main tournament was conducted in a 4-player party PvP, double-elimination format. Introducing a selection ceremony for the first time, where top qualifier teams directly chose their initial opponents, teams engaged in strategic rivalry right from match selection.

Champions Astral defeated GrindSky and Glory in turn before sweeping SUPAHOTCREWXD 2-0 in the Winners’ Bracket Final. Starting the Grand Final with a one-game advantage, they defeated the same opponent 3-1 in the final round to claim the top spot for three consecutive years since 2024. SUPAHOTCREWXD finished as runners-up, with GrindSky taking second place.

Astral’s ‘McVP,’ who is retiring following this tournament, was awarded Final MVP. On winning both the championship and the individual award on his final stage, he stated, “I don’t think it could be any more perfect”. Having maintained their throne alongside the same teammates, Astral cited training adapted to shifting metas and mutual trust without assigning blame as the driving forces behind their three-peat.

On-site and surrounding programs entertained visitors throughout the venue. The event featured a performance by Filipino girl group KAIA, cosplay stage shows, mini-games, and souvenir photo booths, while game-themed merchandise such as keychains, stickers, and acrylic stands welcomed fans. Prior to the tournament, a session was also arranged for direct communication between the developers and players. Fans unable to attend in person watched the tournament via official YouTube, Facebook, and Twitch broadcasts.

The tournament season centered around dedicated servers also contributed to the game’s growth. According to Wemade Connect, revenue for the 30 days following the launch of this year’s FWC server increased nearly fourfold compared to the previous 30 days, and grew by approximately 18% compared to the same period last year. By drawing new and returning players alongside competitors to a server supporting accelerated character progression, the tournament established a structure where the event and the game service grew together.

Both companies also outlined plans to build upon FWC’s success for long-term service. Gala Lab CEO Kim Hyun-su stated that they are reviewing ways to incorporate tournament match data and player feedback into content and PvP balance improvements. Wemade Connect CEO Lee Ho-dae shared plans to develop the tournament’s foundation and content to allow broader participation across more regions and players.

articles.title: Mayon Volcano raised to Alert Level 3 after eruption
articles.summary: Phivolcs warns several municipalities in Albay to expect ashfall, following the ‘moderately explosive’ Mayon Volcano eruption on Friday, October 30

blocks.text: ERUPTION. A moderately explosive eruption is seen at Mayon Volcano in Albay on October 30, 2026.
Phivolcs
Phivolcs warns several municipalities in Albay to expect ashfall, following the ‘moderately explosive’ Mayon Volcano eruption on Friday, October 30

MANILA, Philippines – State volcanologists raised the status of Mayon Volcano in Albay from Alert Level 2 to Alert Level 3 on Friday, October 30, after a “moderately explosive” eruption occurred at 11:53 am.
This means the volcano is in “a new phase of magmatic eruption,” according to the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs).

Friday’s eruption generated an ash plume 3,000 meters or 3 kilometers high above Mayon’s crater. Phivolcs warned the municipalities of Daraga, Camalig, and Guinobatan in Albay, as well as adjacent towns, to expect ashfall.

blocks.caption: Mayon Volcano raised to Alert Level 3 after eruption

blocks.text: In the coming days and weeks, Phivolcs said there will also be “increased chances” of lava flows and hazardous pyroclastic density currents (PDCs) — locally known as uson — affecting the volcano’s upper to middle slopes.

PDCs are made up of fragmented volcanic particles, gases, and ash that travel down volcanic slopes at high speeds. They can destroy or burn anything in their path, with temperatures generally ranging between 200°C and 700°C, according to the United States Geological Survey.
Phivolcs recommended evacuation from the 6-kilometer-radius permanent danger zone surrounding Mayon, citing possible PDCs, lava flows, rockfalls, and other volcanic hazards.
“Increased vigilance against [PDCs], lahars, and sediment-laden streamflows along channels draining the edifice is also advised,” added the agency.
There have been several changes in Mayon’s alert level in 2026.
Last January 1, the volcano was raised from Alert Level 1 to Alert Level 2, then raised further to Alert Level 3 on January 6.
It stayed under Alert Level 3 for around seven months, until it was lowered to Alert Level 2 on August 5, a level it maintained until Friday’s eruption.
The alert levels range from 0 (quiet) to 5 (hazardous eruption in progress). – Rappler.com

articles.title: Crypto giant Binance hit by hack suspected to be largest in history
articles.summary: Two analytics firms have attributed the incident to a North Korean hacking unit called TraderTraitor.

blocks.text: Cryptocurrency giant Binance said on Thursday that $6.3bn (£4.7bn) of digital assets have been impacted by what has been described as the "largest hack in history".
The world's biggest crypto exchange said about half of those assets have been frozen with the help of other platforms, adding that it will "cover all losses".
Early checks show the incident may have involved an engineer's laptop that had been compromised, which allowed an attacker to make unauthorised withdrawals, Binance said.
Two analytics firms have attributed the incident, which eclipses a record-setting $1.5bn hack on the Bybit exchange in 2025, to a North Korean hacking unit called TraderTraitor.
AI-powered investigations company TRM Labs said in a report that several elements of the Binance attack resemble earlier North Korean-linked incidents, including the Bybit hack.
The lab's global head of policy Ari Redbord told the BBC the Binance hack is a "watershed moment" that is unlike anything the industry has seen.
The attacker still holds an enormous sum of stolen assets, meaning efforts to trace and recover the funds are far from over, Redbord added.
Chainalysis, another crypto analytics firm, also said it has "high confidence" that the North Korean group are linked to the hack.
Eric Jardine, Chainalysis' Head of Research, urged every exchange to remain vigilant as the platforms are attractive targets for hackers due to the sheer value of assets.

Binance did not directly respond to BBC queries about the incident's potential links to North Korea but said: "We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice."

The incident concerns Binance.com - while much smaller crypto platform Binance.US, which provides trading services specifically for American residents - said its platform is not affected by the issue.
In a series of posts, Yi He, Binance's co-chief executive, thanked various cryptocurrency issuers for freezing the assets.
"Safety first: withdrawals are currently disabled until the environment is confirmed to be secure," she said.
Two other major crypto platforms, Tether and Circle, said they have frozen a total of about $2.4bn of assets in response to the potential Binance hack.

Circle chief executive Jeremy Allaire said his firm is "closely tracking reports of a potential exploit involving Binance" and that his company has frozen more than $800m in assets linked to the incident.
Circle is the issuer and co-creator of the USDC, one of the world's largest US dollar-backed cryptocurrencies.
Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said his firm has frozen around $1.6bn "related to a potential Binance exchange hack."
"Protecting the industry and our partners is our main priority," said Ardoino, whose company issues a cryptocurrency known as USDT.
World Liberty Financial, a crypto company linked to US President Donald Trump and his family, said it has worked with its partners to freeze stolen funds.
Crypto exchange Coinbase said it was unaffected by the incident and was monitoring the situation.
Several crypto industry observers had flagged concerns about a potential hack on Binance hours before the exchange confirmed the security issue.
Binance, which was founded in China in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide.
The exchange has been subject of regulatory scrutiny around the world.
The company said in 2024 that it has more than $160bn in assets under custody.
Bitcoin dropped by more than 4% following the alerts. The price of other major cryptocurrencies including Ethereum and Solana also fell sharply.

articles.title: How cops are turning Negros classrooms into a frontline vs school violence
articles.summary: Police deploy nearly 200 cops with backgrounds in psychology, teaching, and counseling to help prevent bullying, strengthen school security, and promote mental wellness for 1.4 million junior and…

items: Police Brigadier General Rudecindo Reales initiated the 'CampuSaya' program in Negros Occidental to address school violence and bullying by involving police officers as mentors and lecturers in schools.
The initiative aims to create safer school environments for 1.4 million students through a focus on mental wellness, campus security, and encouraging students to report threats or bullying.
CampuSaya has mobilized nearly 2,000 security volunteers and emphasizes partnerships with local government and parents to foster a supportive community for students.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

NEGROS OCCIDENTAL, Philippines – A father of two high school students, Police Brigadier General Rudecindo Reales had been watching with growing concern as violence swept through school campuses in different parts of the country.
The deadly incidents were far from the Negros Island Region (NIR), but their impact was close enough to worry him about the safety of many of the region’s school children.

When he took over as the region’s police director in early September, Reales began working on an initiative that would take the police beyond their traditional role as security personnel and put them in classrooms to help prevent bullying and violence.

blocks.caption: LIST: Cases of school violence in the Philippines in 2026

blocks.text: The result was “CampuSaya,” a play on the phrase “campus na masaya” (happy campus), which brings together nearly 200 police officers with backgrounds in psychology, teaching, and guidance counseling to reach 1.4 million junior and senior high school students in Negros Occidental, Negros Oriental, and Siquijor.
Using instructional materials designed to address troubled learners, the cops will serve as lecturers and mentors, visiting schools throughout the region until June 2027.
With the slogan “Resilient Minds, Kind Hearts and Zero Hate,” the initiative aims to create safer schools where students feel protected, valued, and free to pursue their dreams.

CampuSaya held its inaugural launch at the Bacolod City National High School (BCNHS) on October 22, followed by another in Talisay City, Negros Occidental, the next day. Launches in Dumaguete City and Siquijor followed on October 29 and 30, respectively.
Reales told Rappler on Wednesday, October 28, that CampuSaya was an initiative unique to the NIR, and it was something he was already planning even before he was assigned as the region’s top cop.
Before taking up the post, he served in the Philippine National Police Civil Security Group (CSG), where he headed the Supervisory Office for Security and Investigation Agencies (SOSIA).
Reales, the relatively new region’s third police director, replaced Brigadier General Romano Cardino, who led the PNP in the NIR nearly four months.

He said CampuSaya was also born out of a father’s fear – the kind that follows reports of children dying in places meant to keep them safe. Beyond his responsibilities as a police chief, he was watching the violence unfold as a parent of two high school students.
“Tatay rin ako (I am also a father). And I am also a bit worried about what happened in school campuses in other parts of the country,” he said.

The incidents were too shocking to be easily forgotten. These were deadly shootings involving young students: three people were killed at Banga National High School in South Cotabato on September 18, two at Ateneo de Zamboanga in Zamboanga City on August 18, and three at San Jose National High School in Tacloban City.

In his first month in the NIR, Reales had to contend with a series of bomb and shooting threats targeting schools in the region. These included schools in the towns of EB Magalona and Isabela, the cities of Victorias, Escalante, Bago, Kabankalan, and Bacolod in Negros Occidental, and Dumaguete in Negros Oriental.
A police assessment identified the need to strengthen physical security in schools to prevent a recurrence of the deadly violence reported in Tacloban, Zamboanga, and South Cotabato.

“That is why we immediately partnered with the Department of Education, local government units, barangay councils, and force multipliers to ensure that all public and private schools in the region are provided with security personnel,” Reales said.
CampuSaya has since mobilized close to 2,000 security volunteers.
“In larger schools with thousands of students,” he added, “we actually provide police personnel as peacekeepers.”
But Reales said keeping intruders and other threats away from school grounds was only part of the challenge.
“Beyond campus security,” Reales stressed, “we also need to ensure the mental wellness of the learners via a holistic approach: CampuSaya.”
The initiative rests on three pillars: strengthening campus security, ensuring student mental wellness, and fostering a culture of reporting.

The third encourages students to report threats or suspicious behavior by fellow students and classmates to school or police authorities. It also seeks to empower them to speak up against bullying rather than remain silent.
By encouraging students to report concerns early, police hope to respond promptly and prevent threats from escalating into violence.
The program also extends beyond school gates through the region’s police community relations offices.

PNP personnel in the region would work with parents, teaching them how to communicate more effectively with their children through meaningful conversations that encourage good behavior. Parents would also learn to recognize warning signs in their children’s behavior.
“Let us turn our concern into action and our partnership into protection,” Reales said.
At BCNHS, principal Richard Gelangre welcomed the program, describing it as an important initiative for the psychosocial well-being of students.
“Together with schools, CampuSaya can guide children to stay away from the bad influences of certain internet games,” Gelangre said.

blocks.caption: Senate approves school safety bill after fatal shootings

blocks.text: Gladys Amylaine Sales, schools division superintendent for Negros Occidental, called CampuSaya as a promising school safety initiative built on meaningful partnerships.

She said the program reflected a shared commitment to building safe, caring, inclusive, and resilient learning communities, while nurturing students who are resilient in mind, kind in heart, and free from hate.

For Reales, the challenge now is to turn that vision into a sustained effort, one that makes schools not only more secure but also places where children feel safe enough to learn, speak up, and grow. – Rappler.com
