articles.title: Elke Sommer, prolific German star of A Shot in the Dark and And Then There Were None, dies aged 85
articles.summary:
The Berlin-born actress had a gift for languages that took her to Hollywood, landing roles alongside Peter Sellers, Dick Van Dyke and Paul Newman

Elke Sommer, the prolific German star of the…

blocks.text: Elke Sommer, the prolific German star of the Pink Panther film A Shot in the Dark, early 70s Agatha Christie adaptation And Then there Were None, and British sex comedy Carry On Behind, has died aged 85. Bild magazine reported that Sommer had died in Los Angeles of heart failure.

German-born Sommer, whose best-known film roles were in the 1960s and 70s, was one of the wave of European performers who crossed over to Hollywood and English-language cinema with considerable success, following the post-war emergence of European New Wave cinema. Sommer was one of the few German actors to make waves at the time, as Hollywood made much of her bombshell image.

blocks.caption: With Paul Newman in The Prize. Photograph: Moviestore/Shutterstock

blocks.text: Born Elke Schletz in 1940 in Berlin, the daughter of a Protestant pastor, she was evacuated with her family to Bavaria during the war. Intending to work as an interpreter, she was spotted by celebrated Italian director Vittorio de Sica after winning a beauty contest on a trip to Italy in 1958, and subsequently offered roles in a string of Italian comedy films. She crossed back into more serious work with the West German drama The Death Ship, opposite Horst Buchholz (who would go on to appear in cowboy classic The Magnificent Seven).

With her gift for languages, Sommer made her first film in English, the 1961 British comedy Don’t Bother to Knock, opposite Richard Todd, and was billed as one of the “six most exciting women in the world” alongside Melina Mercouri, Jeanne Moreau and Romy Schneider in Carl Foreman’s 1963 war fable, The Victors. Sommer’s Hollywood breakthrough arrived in the same year, with The Prize; she was cast as Paul Newman’s lover in an adaptation of Irving Wallace’s hit novel, for which she was a joint winner of a most promising newcomer Golden Globe.

blocks.caption: With Sellers in A Shot in the Dark Photograph: Moviestore/Shutterstock

blocks.text: Sommer’s Hollywood career then took off with A Shot in the Dark, in which she leaned heavily into her “sexpot” image as a maid suspected of a series of murders in the sequel to The Pink Panther. Following its success, Sommer appeared in a string of high profile Hollywood films, including The Art of Love with James Garner and Dick Van Dyke, The Oscar with Stephen Boyd, and the Bob Hope comedy Boy, Did I Get a Wrong Number! In 1968, she achieved leading actor status with The Wicked Dreams of Paula Schultz, a comedy about an East German athlete who pole-vaults over the Berlin Wall.

In the 1970s, Sommer appeared in two cult horror films by Mario Bava, Baron Blood and Lisa and the Devil, and sex comedies Percy and Percy’s Progress for British director Ralph Thomas. She followed these with two high profile British films: as secretary Vera Clyde in And Then There Were None in 1974, adapted from Agatha Christie’s hit novel, and a year later in Carry On Behind, the 27th in the Carry On series.

blocks.caption: Mario Bava’s cult horror Lisa and the Devil from 1973. Photograph: Everett/Shutterstock

blocks.text: After another Peter Sellers film, The Prisoner of Zenda, and Ralph Thomas’s heist film A Nightingale Sang in Berkeley Square, Sommer scaled back her screen appearances and concentrated on painting. In the mid-1980s, she also became embroiled in a long-running feud with Zsa Zsa Gabor after they appeared together on TV show Circus of the Stars; Sommer was ultimately awarded $3.3m in damages for defamation.
Sommer was married twice, to writer Joe Hyams from 1964 until 1981, and hotelier Wolf Walther from 1993 until his death in 2026.

articles.title: India increases growth forecast for fiscal year
articles.summary: India's Ministry of Finance has increased its growth forecasts for the current fiscal year. But it also warned about inflation, particularly for fuel and energy, amid continued instability in the…

image.caption: Despite the ministry's rosy overall forecast, fuel costs have risen by around a quarter in the past year, putting severe strain on households.Image: Diptendu Dutta/NurPhoto/picture alliance

blocks.text: India's Ministry of Finance expects India's economy to grow at a pace of 7.3% in the current fiscal year based on its latest assessment of current data, it said in its October economic review.
The estimate is a slight increase on the previous forecast of 7.1%.
India's current fiscal year, known as FY27, runs from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027.
The report contrasted these figures with global growth predictions of nearer 3%, saying "India's growth momentum, by comparison, has held firm."
The ministry said growth in various key indicators like energy consumption, port traffic, goods and services tax (GST) collections, and car sales had accelerated in the previous quarter.
Inflation, fueled by El Nino and geopolitics, poses a threat

However, the ministry also warned of continued inflationary pressure and pressure on the rupee currency, as well as downside risks from the El Nino weather phonemenon that could threaten soil moisture ahead of the winter sowing season.

It said that external factors like oil prices and "global uncertainties" — seemingly a reference at least in part to the instablity in the Middle East — continued to pressure the rupee's value and pose inflationary risks.
Consumer price inflation (CPI), the wholesale price index (WPI), food cost prices and fuel and power prices were all rising month for month, albeit at very different rates.
The CPI was up 5.54% year-on-year in September, but the WPI had risen more sharply at 11.39%. Food index inflation was up by 8% in rural areas, and a slightly more modest 7.18% in urban centers.

But, as in many other countries, fuel and power costs increases were in an entirely different league, at 25.85% inflation in September 2026 comapred to the same month a year earlier, prior to the outbreak of fighting in the Middle East.
Ministry says FX reserves ample, rupee's decline appears manageable

Although it has been a comparatively slow decline, the rupee has been consistently losing value against the US dollar over the past five years, threatening the country's relative purchasing power internationally. This slide has picked up pace in the last 15 months or so.
But the ministry pointed to foreign exchange reserves worth some $721 billion and said that India was "well-positioned" to weather such risks and sustain its expansionary trajectory..

articles.title: China leaders demand more loyalty and more initiative
articles.summary: The CCP session emphasized internal discipline — as expected, but left the question of Xi Jinping's successor unanswered. The party seems anxious of any instability as geopolitics heats up and…

image.caption: Xi Jinping (center) serves as both the head of state and the general secretary of the ruling Communist Party in ChinaImage: Li Xiang/Xinhua/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: The top echelon of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) held a four-day session behind closed doors in Beijing this week, with the talks focusing on strict leadership and discipline inside the ruling party.

Xi Jinping, who is both the CCP's general secretary and the head of state in China, signaled he would not only deepen the existing anti-corruption effort, but also ensure that party officials demonstrate more loyalty and more initiative at all levels.

According to the press release published on Thursday, the committee published a resolution praising the leadership and Xi Jinping for "enormous political courage and strong sense of responsibility" in tackling the issues of corruption and the weakening of the Party's governance.
The statement emphasized the need to "consistently advance comprehensive and strict Party leadership."
China's leadership fears instability
Kerry Brown, head of the Lau China Institute at King's College London, says Xi wants to minimize potential sources of instability.

Amid the current international tensions and the internal problems in China, including economic difficulties, Xi is pursuing his anti-corruption campaign and by demanding loyalty. "This is just going to intensify because if [the CCP] isn't disciplined and united, the party believes that it will go the same way as everywhere else in the world at the moment and become disunited and unstable," Brown told DW.
Trump, Putin or Xi: Who really runs the world?
'Two-faced' party members targeted by Xi
Xi also recently spoke of the necessity to identify and remove "two-faced functionaries" from the political system.

In his speech, which was published in mid-October by the party's Qiushi Magazine, Xi referred to people professing loyalty to the central leadership while working against its instructions and following their own "individualistic" goals. The Chinese president described them as "political opportunists." He also criticized party officials pretending to be "nice guys," as in, those who use harmony as an excuse to stand aside when problems arise.

Brown points out that China's political system is now facing a crucial dilemma: If officials at all levels are now indeed expected to show innovation and courage in solving problems, the party's control could grow weak. This could, in turn, boost corruption.

However, if CCP leaders lean more on the "strict Party leadership" aspect and ramp up the pressure on the rank-and-file, there is also the danger of suppressing initiative. This could go beyond the party itself and could even affect the military.
The party is "very, very risk averse," Brown points out.
China 'kind of works' in a messy world
Chong Ja Ian, a political scientist at the National University of Singapore, notes that party functionaries under Xi only have a limited space to make their own decisions.
Taking this into account, the party's push for individuals to show initiative is not necessarily a major issue.

"I believe Xi would like for the officials to act proactively and decisively by conducting specific tasks; but he still doesn't want them thinking for themselves so much that they can question the agenda he prescribed. The 'proactivity' demanded by Xi is limited to the implementation, not decision-making," he told DW.
Brown adds that Xi seems to be ready to sacrifice a certain amount of operational flexibility to gain more control and stability.
"As long as you have unity, you live for another day, right? But if you have disunity, you probably die the same day," he told DW.
This approach "kind of works," at least at the moment, he added.
"It's not like the Chinese economy is disastrous. It's not great, but it's not disastrous. In any case, look at the outside world. It's a mess."
New World Dis-Order: Is the age of peace and stability over?
Who will succeed Xi Jinping?
Outside observers are also focusing on Xi's future and possible successors for the 73-year-old leader.
For now, Xi seems to be firmly in control. It is highly likely that he would be confirmed as the party's general secretary next fall, and could stay in that position until 2032.
This is due to the changes pushed by Xi in 2018, which removed term limits for state and party leaders.
Both analysts told DW that the issue of succession plays a major role in Xi's push towards internal stability.

"There's always a danger of differences in the party fragmenting it, especially when the question of succession comes up," says Brown. "And even though we don't expect to see a successor anytime soon, you know, there's going to be speculation about who might succeed Xi."
"He can't go on forever," he added.
How Xi Jinping's authoritarianism is killing China's economy
Political scientist Chong Ja Ian says that Xi currently holds all the power. Therefore, the CCP leader could be afraid of his authority being undermined if he named a successor ahead of time.

"On the other hand, a failure to make preparations on time could create a power vacuum that can cause major instability," he told DW. "To solve this dilemma, the current leader needs to have both the necessary self-confidence and the readiness to take a step back — just like his predecessors did. But not everyone has that kind of confidence."
This text was originally published in Chinese.

articles.summary: Self-described ‘Crypto King’ Aiden Pleterski was found guilty of fraud over $5,000 by the jury at his Toronto trial Thursday morning.

image.caption: Self-described 'Crypto King' Aiden Pleterski has been found guilty of fraud. (aiden.ptrs/Instagram)

blocks.text: Toronto·Breaking
Self-described ‘Crypto King’ Aiden Pleterski was found guilty of fraud over $5,000 by the jury at his Toronto trial Thursday morning.
Pleterski represented himself, was denied a mistrial earlier this week
Pleterski, who represented himself at trial, appeared emotional after the verdict was read in Ontario Superior Court.
The jury began deliberations around 10:30 a.m. and came back with their verdict 10 minutes before noon.
More to come.

articles.title: Bernardo: Only Ping not involved in infra kickbacks
articles.summary: Former Department of Public Works and Highways undersecretary Roberto Bernardo testified yesterday that to his knowledge, only Sen. Panfilo Lacson was not involved in any kickback scheme surrounding…

blocks.text: October 30, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Former Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) undersecretary Roberto Bernardo testified yesterday that to his knowledge, only Sen. Panfilo Lacson was not involved in any kickback scheme surrounding government infrastructure projects.
Bernardo made the revelation upon the questioning of Associate Justice Ronald Moreno whether there were proponents of projects who did not receive commitment fees or kickbacks.
“Do you know a proponent that did not get a kickback? Do heroes still exist?” Moreno asked.
“I don’t know of any congressman who was offered and declined. Only Sen. Lacson did not have any commitment,” Bernardo said.
When asked by Associate Justice Karl Miranda if all projects of the DPWH have proponents and kickbacks, Bernardo said yes.
Bernardo, however, said he did not have direct dealings with former House speaker Martin Romualdez regarding kickbacks and projects.
Bernardo also testified that former senator Nancy Binay was allocated 12 to 15 percent of commitment fees from projects while former senator Grace Poe was allotted 20 percent.
The commitment fees of Sen. Jinggoy Estrada, meanwhile, amounted to 18 to 25 percent.
He also named a certain Carlo Aguilar, whom he described as a cousin of Sen. Mark Villar, the former DPWH secretary, who was allotted five percent of a P500-million lump sum fund from the department.
He said Aguilar approached him and asked if there were funds that could be released and signed off to Villar.
Bernardo said he had seen Villar and Aguilar together on several occasions.
Meanwhile, Bernardo said he split the remaining five percent with the late former DPWH undersecretary Maria Catalina Cabral.
Martin cleared
Bernardo testified before the Sandiganbayan that ex-speaker and Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez did not request from him a list of infrastructure projects in exchange for kickbacks.

During the hearing before the anti-graft court’s Third Division on the bail petition of Romualdez over a P7.4-billion plunder case, Bernardo said that in his affidavits, he did not mention Romualdez asking for projects from him.
He also clarified that he did not refer to Romualdez as a proponent of government projects.
Bernardo, however, admitted receiving financial benefits from infrastructure projects associated with various proponents, which he called “balato” or token.

Bernardo said Alcantara and then DPWH National Capital Region director Gerard Opulencia would provide the list of projects for proponent lawmakers for funding, and would also collect commitment fees from contractors since this will serve as kickback for the proponents.
More deliveries

Bernardo’s former aide, Vergel Nino Garcia, in a separate hearing, testified that he made deliveries of suitcases and boxes to suspended Senator Estrada, former senator Ramon Revilla Jr. and former DPWH chief Manuel Bonoan, among others.

Garcia made the testimony during the hearing before the Sandiganbayan Fifth Division on Estrada’s petition for bail over his P573-million plunder charge over alleged kickbacks from flood control projects.
Garcia said he delivered 12 boxes intended for Estrada at the Artiaga Building in San Juan City in November 2024 upon the instruction of Bernardo.
He said he was accompanied by Bernardo’s driver, Francisco dela Fuente.
Garcia, however, admitted that he did not see the contents of the boxes nor did he take photos or videos of the delivery.
Garcia said he also made deliveries to Revilla, Bonoan, Cabral and former education undersecretary Trygve Olaivar.

Former DPWH NCR director Opulencia, meanwhile, testified that there is a 5 to 10 percent kickback called “pasasalamat” (gratitude) for DPWH officials, on top of the 25 percent “commitment” fees, which he believed came from private contractors.
The DPWH will stand by and honor the multibillion-peso infrastructure allocations in the national budget, Public Works Secretary Giovanni Lopez said. – Rainier Allan Ronda

articles.title: Leasing program to ease classroom shortage .
articles.summary: The Department of Education is leasing available private school facilities and properties and using them to address classroom shortages.

blocks.text: October 30, 2026 | 12:00am

In a statement released yesterday, Education Secretary Sonny Angara said DepEd is expanding its infrastructure strategy to include the leasing of available, compliant private school facilities and properties as a solution to urban classroom congestion.
STAR / File
MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Education (DepEd) is leasing available private school facilities and properties and using them to address classroom shortages.
This is also a way to bypass multi-year construction delays and provide immediate relief to overcrowded campuses.
Angara explained that leasing serves as an agile, high-impact solution alongside traditional building projects to meet urgent classroom needs on the ground.

The initiative is part of DepEd’s infrastructure strategy which works alongside Department of Public Works and Highways-led construction, local government unit partnerships, Public-Private Partnerships, DepEd Learning Continuity Spaces and collaborations with other organizations.
“We cut down waiting times significantly, decongest our public campuses and ensure our learners are sitting comfortably in classrooms rather than makeshift spaces,” Angara said.
The leasing program targets highly congested public campuses across key cities and regions.
Initially, DepEd selected Baliwag and Marikina as models for accelerating learning space expansion.
DepEd offices are currently evaluating additional campus leases, ensuring that safety, accessibility and proximity standards are strictly met.

articles.title: More drug war victims’ kin want to join Duterte trial
articles.summary: Almost 100 relatives of drug war victims have applied to participate in the ongoing crimes against humanity trial of former president Rodrigo Duterte before the International Criminal Court.

blocks.text: October 30, 2026 | 12:00am
Photos courtesy of the International Criminal Court show former president Rodrigo Duterte during his first in-person appearance before the tribunal since his arrest in March 2025.
Photos / ICC | via Janvic Mateo

MANILA, Philippines — Almost 100 relatives of drug war victims have applied to participate in the ongoing crimes against humanity trial of former president Rodrigo Duterte before the International Criminal Court (ICC).
According to the ICC Registry, it received an additional 46 applications comprising 96 individuals classified under “Group A” or those who “clearly qualify” as victims in the case.
Their applications were formally transmitted to the ICC Trial Chamber III on Oct. 28.
Marked as confidential, details of the applications were not released to the public.
Earlier, the Pre-Trial Chamber I authorized 539 individual applicants to participate in the proceedings.
Authorized victims are not necessarily witnesses for the prosecution, which is in charge of presenting evidence to prove that the alleged crimes were committed by the respondents.
Instead, the authorized victims are allowed by the ICC to participate and present their views during the proceedings through their common legal representatives.
They may also be granted reparations if an accused is found guilty by the court.
The ICC earlier adopted an “A-B-C Approach” in the victim admission process for the proceedings.
Those classified as Group B are the ones who “clearly do not qualify” as victims, while Group C is for those “whom the Registry could not make a clear determination for any reason.”
It remains unclear if there were additional applicants under Group C.

In addition to victims during the Duterte administration’s drug war, the judges earlier ruled that victims of murder or attempted murder in the Davao area from Nov. 1, 2011 to June 30, 2016 also fall within the scope of the Duterte case.

The case against the former president includes killings in relation to activities of the so-called Davao death squad, along with the broader war on drugs until 2019, when the Philippines officially withdrew from the international tribunal.
Duterte’s trial will begin on Nov. 30 in The Hague, where he has been detained since his arrest in March 2025.

articles.title: Church: Don’t bring home urns for Undas
articles.summary: The Catholic Church discourages bringing home urns during the observance of All Saints’ Day and All Souls’ Day, Manila Cathedral vice rector Fr. Vicente Gabriel Bautista said yesterday.

blocks.text: October 30, 2026 | 12:00am

Bautista reacted to a Facebook post of the Mandaluyong City government announcing that families are allowed to bring home the urns of their departed loved ones that are in the Ash Repository of the columbarium of the Garden of Life Memorial Park.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — The Catholic Church discourages bringing home urns during the observance of All Saints’ Day and All Souls’ Day, Manila Cathedral vice rector Fr. Vicente Gabriel Bautista said yesterday.
According to the announcement, the relatives could retrieve the urns from Oct. 22-29 and should return these on Nov. 5.
The purpose was reportedly to lessen the number of people going to the cemeteries and give families the opportunity to show their respect to their dead relatives.
But Bautista said that even if it would only be for a short period of time, an urn that has already been placed in the niche should no longer be brought home.
“That is why we say ‘rest in peace’. We want them to rest in the peace of the Lord, away from the noise,” he said. “The place of the dead in the cemeteries and columbaries, that place is for them.”
Meanwhile, two weather disturbances are being monitored ahead of the Undas long weekend, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration said yesterday.
A low-pressure area (LPA) is being monitored inside the Philippine area of responsibility (PAR), last located at 825 kilometers east of Eastern Visayas.
Weather specialist Benison Estareja said that the LPA is unlikely to develop into a tropical cyclone in the next 24 hours.
A tropical depression has also developed outside PAR and was last located 3,185 kms east of Central Luzon.
Estareja said that the tropical cyclone is not yet expected to make landfall, affect weather conditions or enter PAR in the coming days. – Josiah Antonio

articles.title: Shortlist of CJ, associate justicebets submitted
articles.summary: The Judicial and Bar Council has submitted to President Marcos its shortlist of five candidates to the position of chief justice.

blocks.text: October 30, 2026 | 12:00am
MANILA, Philippines - The Judicial and Bar Council (JBC) has submitted to President Marcos its shortlist of five candidates to the position of chief justice.

In JBC’s shortlist are Supreme Court Senior Associate Justice Marvic Leonen and Associate Justices Alfredo Benjamin Caguioa, Rodil Zalameda, Japar Dimaampao and Jose Midas Marquez, the SC said in a statement yesterday.
Leonen, Caguioa and Zalameda were “invited” by the JBC to apply due to their seniority, while Dimaampao and Marquez received endorsements of their applications from their supporters.
The President is expected to announce his choice within 90 days after Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo retires on his 70th birthday on Nov. 6.

Zalameda was earlier reported as Marcos’ choice for the next chief justice, but this was denied by Malacañang. It was Zalameda who penned the decision that overturned former first lady Imelda Marcos’ conviction on seven counts of graft by the Sandiganbayan.

Meanwhile, the JBC’s shortlist of aspirants for the next SC associate justice includes Court of Appeals Presiding Justice Fernanda Lampas Peralta, and CA Associate Justices Ramon Bato Jr., Ramon Cruz, Maria Elisa Sempio Diy, Myra Garcia-Fernandez, Ronaldo Roberto Martin and Walter Ong; and Court of Tax Appeals Associate Justice Maria Rowena Modesto-San Pedro.

Solicitor General Darlene Marie Berberabe, Commission on Audit Chairman Gamaliel Cordoba, and Commission on Elections Commissioner Ernesto Maceda Jr. are also on the shortlist of candidates for the position of SC associate justice.
President Marcos’ choice for the next SC associate justice will replace outgoing SC Associate Justice Amy Lazaro-Javier, who will retire on Nov. 16.
His previous appointee to an SC post was Associate Justice Raul Villanueva, in June 2025. Villanueva is currently the most junior in the 15-member bench.

articles.title: Business groups urge removal of insertions
articles.summary: Over 30 business groups are urging Congress leaders to remove baseless insertions in the proposed 2027 budget as well as restore funding for foreign-assisted projects and the EDSA Busway.

blocks.text: October 30, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Over 30 business groups are urging Congress leaders to remove baseless insertions in the proposed 2027 budget as well as restore funding for foreign-assisted projects and the EDSA Busway.

“We call on the leaders of both Houses of Congress – Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian, House Speaker Faustino Dy III, Senate Finance committee chair Joseph Victor Ejercito and House Appropriations committee chair Mikaela Angela Suansing – to remove from the proposed P7.2 trillion 2027 national budget every congressional insertion that has no technical basis,” the business groups said in a joint statement yesterday.

The groups that signed the joint statement are Alyansa Agrikultura, Cebu Business Club, Cebu Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Cebu Leads Foundation, Connected Women, Employers Confederation of the Philippines, Federation of Filipino Chinese-Chambers of Commerce and Industry Inc., Federation of Philippine Industries (FPI), Filipina CEO Circle, Financial Executives Institute of the Philippines, Fintech Alliance.Ph, Foundation for Economic Freedom, Iloilo Economic Development Foundation, Institute for Solidarity in Asia, Institute of Corporate Directors, Investment House Association of the Philippines, Justice Reform Initiative, Makati Business Club, Management Association of the Philippines, Move As One Coalition, Movement for Restoration of Peace and Order, Nextgen Organization of Women Corporate Directors, Parish Pastoral Council for Responsible Voting, People Management Association of the Philippines, Philippine Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Philippine Energy Efficiency Alliance, Philippine Exporters Confederation, Philippine Financial and Inter-Industry Pride, Philippine Institute of Certified Public Accountants, Philippine Retailers Association, Procurement and Supply Institute of Asia, Roundtable for Inclusive Development, Shareholders’ Association of the Philippines, The Outstanding Women in the Nation’s Service Foundation and Women Business Council.

For the business groups, an item should only be in the budget if it is backed by a feasibility study or detailed engineering design and validated as ready for implementation, consistent with the implementing agency’s master plans.

Various sectors have raised concerns over massive insertions in the proposed House General Appropriations Bill approved on third reading earlier this month. Concerns include the more than P180 billion in Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) allocations added in the budget amendments and review subcommittee.

Based on a report by independent budget watchdogs, the additions cover at least 6,000 projects, bringing the DPWH project count in the National Expenditure Program (NEP) to at least 16,000, with many appearing as lump sums for multipurpose buildings and access and bypass roads, without published project lists or proponents.
P130 billion FAP cut
Such additions are to be funded in part by cutting about P130 billion from FAP, P9.5 billion from calamity funds, P1.76 billion from the EDSA Busway and P4.9 billion from health programs.

“We find this deeply troubling. Foreign-assisted projects are the country’s most rigorously prepared infrastructure – backed by feasibility studies, financing commitments and international procurement standards,” the groups said.
The reduced funding would delay high-impact projects intended to help attract investments and bring down logistics costs.
In addition, the groups said raiding calamity funds cannot be justified in a country exposed to disasters.
The groups also urged Congress leaders to strike special provisions that allow agencies to modify or replace projects after enactment.

For transparency, the groups also said amendments should be published in full by identifying the project, location, amount, source of funds, justification and the legislator who proposed it, before the Senate votes on second reading and before the bicameral conference begins.
In addition, the group said no new items must be added at the level of the bicameral conference committee, which should only reconcile what each chamber has already approved.
“Our call is not for delay. We support the timely passage of the 2027 budget and oppose a reenacted budget,” the groups said, noting that a clean and timely budget can coexist.

A budget free of politically driven insertions, they added, would strengthen investor confidence, protect the country’s fiscal space and ensure that every peso spent goes to what the country truly needs.
No to reenacted budget
Gatchalian told reporters on the sidelines of the FPI’s Philippines Business Summit 2026 yesterday that the goal is to avoid a reenacted budget scenario.
“We cannot afford a reenacted budget,” he said, citing the country’s slow economic growth.

Second quarter economic growth was at 2.3 percent, the weakest in five years. This brought average growth in the first half to 2.6 percent, below the government’s 3.5 to 4.5 percent growth target for the year.
“If we reenact the budget, we won’t have new infrastructure… If you don’t have new infrastructure, you don’t have a driver for growth,” Gatchalian said.
On FAP, he said the Senate is looking at restoring some funding, particularly for transportation projects including subway and commuter rail.
“We’re coordinating with the Department of Transportation in that regard,” he said.
“In the NEP, there’s no more allocation. So we’re also studying the possibility of allocating for the EDSA Busway. It’s a good project,” he pointed out.
Given the tight fiscal space, he said the Senate is scrutinizing the budget and is thinking of cutting funding for unnecessary items like travel expenses, seminars and conferences across agencies.
Similar to last year, he said that all movements in the bicameral conference committee would be made public and posted on the website.
“We have three weeks to do the assessment. But we’ve already started… So we’ll have a committee report by the second to third week of November,” he said.

At a briefing in Bukidnon, Palace press officer Claire Castro said it was “premature” for Caloocan Rep. Edgar Erice to describe as “callousness” a proposal to allocate more than P4 billion in public works projects to Ilocos Norte’s first district, represented by President Marcos’ son, House Majority Leader Sandro Marcos.
“Even if it has been proposed, it doesn’t mean that the entire P4 billion will be provided. The process is not yet over,” Castro said.

“When one claims that there is callousness, there should be evidence that the fund was used for corruption. These statements are too premature and can affect the mindset of our countrymen. The budget has been approved at the House, but it doesn’t mean it would be stolen,” she added.
Castro said the President would not allow projects without details, emphasizing that the approval was made by the House of Representatives and not by the executive branch.

“So to those monitoring the budget, we need your help. You won’t do damage to the government. If you notice something that needs to be addressed, tell us and the President will listen. But do not use coarse language, especially if you are a lawmaker,” she said.

Meanwhile, Baguio City Mayor Benjamin Magalong has accused in a television program some politicians of receiving commissions of 20 percent to 30 percent from infrastructure projects, possibly to build up campaign funds for the 2028 elections.

“Look at the political capital of politicians. Assistance is one. The projects, especially those where they have a cut of around 20 percent to 30 percent,” Magalong said. - Alexis Romero, Artemio Dumlao

articles.title: Homilies must come from faith, not AI – Tagle
articles.summary: Cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle, dean of the College of Cardinals, has cautioned against the use of artificial intelligence in preparing Catholic homilies.

blocks.text: October 30, 2026 | 12:00am
Cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle.
interaksyon / Vatican Media via CBCP News
MANILA, Philippines — Cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle, dean of the College of Cardinals, has cautioned against the use of artificial intelligence in preparing Catholic homilies.
CBCPNews reported that Cardinal Tagle said that Catholic homilies and spiritual reflections must come from faith and not from AI.

Speaking before more than 6,000 people gathered during mass for the 75th anniversary of the Diocese of Legazpi held Wednesday at the St. Gregory the Great Cathedral in Legazpi City, Albay, the cardinal said the preaching must flow from personal faith and an encounter with Jesus.
Evangelization, he said, requires people to share their own experience of Christ.
“If it does not come from the heart, that is not a homily,” Tagle said.
He said AI-generated preaching was only a reorganization of existing information rather than a personal testimony of faith.
Tagle’s message echoed Pope Leo XIV, who had urged priests to resist using AI to write their homilies, saying it cannot replace the personal sharing of faith.

articles.title: DENR: Restoring wetlands, rivers vital amid El Niño
articles.summary: The restoration of critical wetlands, rivers and coral reefs in protecting communities is critical against the “very strong” El Niño, Environment Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna said…

blocks.text: October 30, 2026 | 12:00am
To address the concern, the Department of Environment and Natural Resources launched a nationwide ecosystem restoration program to mitigate the impacts of extreme dry heat.
Philstar.com / Dominique Nicole Flores

MANILA, Philippines — The restoration of critical wetlands, rivers and coral reefs in protecting communities is critical against the “very strong” El Niño, Environment Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna said yesterday.

“We are ensuring that our ecosystems remain functional buffers against extreme heat. Protecting our wetlands, rivers, and reefs nationwide is one way of protecting the communities and ensuring environmental survival,” the DENR chief said.

In Caraga, the Protected Area Management Office of the Agusan Marsh Wildlife Sanctuary implemented strict ecosystem-based adaptation measures to protect peatlands and freshwater wetlands which act as natural sponges that regulate water flow, store massive amounts of carbon, and cool surrounding areas to protect communities against extreme heat.

In the National Capital Region and Central Luzon, the DENR’s Manila Bay Site Coordinating and Management Office (MBSCMO) intensified river cleanup and waterway maintenance activities under the Manila Bay Rehabilitation Initiative.

In partnership with the Department of Labor and Employment’s Tulong Panghanapbuhay sa Ating Disadvantaged or Displaced Workers program, the MBSCMO deployed River Rangers for a 10-day cleanup operation along river channels, creeks and estuaries in Pampanga – removing 98,618.93 kilograms of solid waste from trash traps and riverbanks.

The MBSCMO continues to monitor water supply sources, rivers, and creek tributaries in Bulacan, Pampanga, Nueva Ecija, Bataan and Tarlac. In the Bicol Region, DENR-PENRO Masbate identified shallow coral areas and seagrass beds in Mobo and San Jacinto vulnerable to extreme heat.
‘Ready for any eventuality’
The Philippines is ready for any eventuality, Malacañang said yesterday as foreign governments have urged citizens to prepare for possible disasters and other emergency situations.

Japan and some European countries have urged their citizens to stockpile essential supplies and brace for disasters as concerns mount over geopolitical tensions, possible threats from hostile states and cyber-attacks that may disrupt the operations of public utilities.

Meanwhile, during the launch of a nationwide school-based hydroponics project, Education Secretary Sonny Angara said investing in hydroponic gardening is a solution to shortage in food and water that might be aggravated by a prolonged super El Niño. – Alexis Romero, Evelyn Macairan, Marc Jayson Cayabyab

articles.title: Palace: World getting smaller for Bato
articles.summary: The world is getting smaller for fugitive Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa, Malacañang said yesterday, as it gave assurance that authorities are looking into all credible leads that…

blocks.text: October 30, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The world is getting smaller for fugitive Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa, Malacañang said yesterday, as it gave assurance that authorities are looking into all credible leads that could lead to his arrest.

The Philippine National Police (PNP) has given Dela Rosa, who has a standing International Criminal Court (ICC) arrest warrant for alleged crimes against humanity, one week to surrender, an ultimatum that expires today.

Dela Rosa, a former police chief who enforced the Duterte administration’s bloody drug war, is now being tracked by his former subordinates and has been in hiding since November last year. The government has offered a P50-million bounty for information leading to his arrest.

“The combined effect of heightened police operations increase public awareness and the bounty announcement has substantially narrowed the senator’s ability to move freely without drawing attention,” Palace press officer Claire Castro said in a media briefing, quoting the PNP and the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG).
“Indeed, the world of Senator Bato is getting smaller because those who will see him may provide information immediately to the PNP and other law enforcement agencies,” she added.
Castro said National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag has also received information about the possible whereabouts of the senator.

The task force led by PNP deputy chief for administration Lt. Gen. Joseph Lopez is ensuring seamless coordination among all concerned agencies to ensure that every relevant piece of information is properly validated and acted upon, she added.
“What we can assure the public is that all information received is being carefully and thoroughly assessed and credible leads are being acted upon without delay,” Castro said.

“The PNP, guided by the direction of the (secretary of the DILG), will continue to carry out its mandate professionally, lawfully and with full respect for due process while protecting the integrity of its ongoing operation,” Castro said.
PNP eyes wanted posters
The PNP is still studying whether to put up wanted posters of Dela Rosa.
According to PNP spokesman Col. Allen Rae Co, there is no need to put up a wanted poster of the senator for now.
“We do not see any need for now because first, who does not know who Senator Bato is?” Co said in a news briefing at Camp Crame.
Co added that Dela Rosa should consider turning himself over to the authorities to avoid a possible armed encounter which could lead to casualties.
“Let’s avoid any untoward incident, any potential dangerous encounters or any harm that may come to anybody,” Co said.
As Dela Rosa has yet to surrender 91 guns registered under his name, the PNP considers him “armed and dangerous.”
Return the bounty
The NBI will return to the government the P50-million reward for Dela Rosa’s arrest if its agents capture the lawmaker, Matibag said.
Matibag said the bureau could claim the bounty if it apprehended Dela Rosa but would likely return the money for public service, joking that it could instead go to the NBI’s retirement fund.
Law enforcement agencies and their members are not supposed to collect bounties.

“I am not the one to discuss the bounty because it is not for us. If we catch him, we will probably claim the bounty but then give it back to the government for public service,” Matibag told reporters, adding the NBI might consider donating the money to the agency’s retirement fund.

The P50-million reward was announced by Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla on Oct. 23 as authorities intensified the manhunt for Dela Rosa, who has been in hiding since May 14 after an ICC arrest warrant against him was made public.
The PNP has given the senator until today to surrender, warning it is prepared to enforce the warrant if he refuses.
Both the PNP and NBI have formed dedicated tracker teams to locate the senator and is pursuing leads on his whereabouts.– Emmanuel Tupas, Mark Ernest Villeza

blocks.text: US intelligence agencies believe the Nvidia chief executive, Jensen Huang, has been targeted by a Chinese spy who had done business with him, according to a new report by the New York Times.

Alice Huang or Huang Le, of no relation to the Nvidia CEO, is an executive at a Singapore-based datacenter company called Megaspeed. She had previously been suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China, prompting American officials to surveil and monitor her. Those officials have determined that she was acting as a Chinese intelligence asset, passing commercial information to Beijing, the New York Times reported, citing unnamed sources.

In the course of their surveillance, American officials determined that Alice Huang developed a close relationship with Nvidia’s CEO, according to the Times. Nvidia’s powerful chips serve as a cornerstone of the AI boom and have vaulted Jensen Huang into one of the most influential leadership positions in the industry. In that position, he has developed a close partnership with Donald Trump as the US government attempts to defend its position as a leader in AI development.
White House officials are reportedly alarmed by Alice Huang’s access to the head of Nvidia precisely because of the close relationship he’s developed with Trump, according to the New York Times.

The Trump administration has imposed restrictions on exports of advanced AI chips to China as a matter of national security. Megaspeed’s Huang was suspected to have been helping the government get around those restrictions.
In a statement to the New York Times, Nvidia said there was nothing out of the ordinary about the Nvidia CEO’s interactions with Alice Huang.
after newsletter promotion

“Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” the spokesperson said in a statement. Megaspeed and customers like it “receive ordinary business information – not sensitive Nvidia trade secrets – and zero information relevant to national security”.

articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro calls himself 'leader of Brazil' after election loss
articles.summary: The defeated presidential candidate says he will lead the opposition from the US.

blocks.text: The defeated candidate in Brazil's presidential election, Flávio Bolsonaro, has referred to himself as "leader of Brazil" in a letter he published on social media after leaving the country for the United States.
Bolsonaro lost to his left-wing rival, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, in the run-off on Sunday by a difference of 4.4 million votes, but has not conceded defeat.
In the letter, Bolsonaro alleges, without offering evidence, that he was the victim of "electoral fraud" and says that he will lead the opposition from the US.
He left Brazil on Tuesday after failing to comply with an order to surrender his passports, a decision which Lula described as "a shameful act".
Bolsonaro starts his letter, which he posted on his X account, saying "I address the Brazilian people and the international community as the leader of Brazil".
However, he had posted a previous version, that was later deleted, in which he wrote: "I address the Brazilian people and the international community as the rightful president of Brazil."
Both versions repeat the allegation that Bolsonaro first made on election night, that an extension of polling hours on Sunday had benefited his rival.
In the letter, he says it was "an electoral fraud unfolding before my eyes".

The extension was requested by both Lula's and Bolsonaro's campaign teams, and the head of Brazil's electoral authority has said that the vote proceeded normally and in full accordance with the country's laws and constitution.

An analysis of election data conducted by BBC Brazil and BBC Verify has also found that only around 34,000 people voted during the extended hours - far lower than the 4.4 million votes that separated Lula from Bolsonaro.
In his letter, Bolsonaro also addresses his departure from Brazil - which caused confusion after he disappeared for more than 24 hours.
It later emerged that he had gone across the land border to Argentina, and from there flew on to Florida, following a brief refuelling stop in Ecuador.

The trip of Lazaro, who is also Special Envoy of the ASEAN Chair, coincided with the 70th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the Philippines and Myanmar.

"Over seven decades, friendly relations between the Philippines and Myanmar have grown not only through official exchanges, but also through people-to-people ties. The humanitarian mission builds on this longstanding relationship connection while carrying forward the Philippines’ responsibilities as ASEAN Chair in 2026," the DFA said.

articles.title: Germany seeks new head of state
articles.summary: Who should become Germany's new president? That question is becoming pressing. Many want to see Germany's first female head of state. Chancellor Friedrich Merz is keeping his cards close to his chest.

image.caption: Frank-Walter Steinmeier is set to leave office early next yearImage: Katharina Kausche/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Wanted: A new head of state — female, male, or other. Requirements: German citizen, entitled to vote, minimum age 40. Please apply as soon as possible! Availability starting January 30, 2027; job starts March 19, 2027.

This is not an official job posting, but Germany's federal government is indeed looking for someone to fill the nation's highest office. Having already served two terms, current President Frank-Walter Steinmeier is no longer eligible for another, leaving the position open for a successor. Many feel that it is time for Germany's first-ever female head of state.

"The person should have a certain level of public recognition, be politically unbiased, capable of bringing people together, approachable and a reasonably good [public] speaker," political scientist Ursula Münch told DW.

In Germany, a federal parliamentary republic, the president serves as head of state and a representative of the country as well as someone who embodies moral authority for the nation. Unlike for instance in the US, France, or Russia, the president does not wield extensive political power or direct government affairs.

Steinmeier was nominated by his own party, the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD), in 2009. However, once elected via a convention of parliamentarians and state electors, a president-elect has to suspend their party membership in order to serve in the office apolitically. This time, it is Chancellor Friedrich Merz's center-right Christian Democrats (CDU), the power broker in the coalition government with the SPD and the conservative Christian Social Union (CSU), which has the right to nominate a candidate.

Political scientist Münch says that "the three parties must agree on a person who is acceptable for all three." Since the convention that will select Steinmeier's successor is currently controlled by these three parties and their delegates, it is very likely that whoever Merz nominates will be elected.

blocks.caption: Senior CSU politician Ilse Aigner is thought to have a good chance of succeeding SteinmeierImage: Chris Emil Janßen/IMAGO

blocks.text: Will Germany soon have its first female president?

"Well, I would really like it to be a woman this time. We've had 12 male federal presidents since 1949 — it's about time for a woman! But if the right man were to be nominated, I'd be fine with that too," says Münch. According to an August poll conducted by the Forsa polling institute for the RTL television network, about 74% of German respondents say they don't care whether it's a man or a woman. Another 19% explicitly want a woman, while 5% prefer a man.

Bavarian politician Ilse Aigner appears to have a good chance. She is president of the Bavarian State Parliament in Munich. Aigner is a member of the smallest party in the coalition, the Bavarian CSU, and is considered a unifying figure. She also has experience in government in Berlin, having served as agricultural minister at the federal level. She enjoys strong support within her Bavarian CSU party, whose leader Markus Söder recently said: "It would be tremendous if she became federal president."

Even members of the opposition Greens and the SPD are full of praise for Aigner's candidacy. "What are we actually waiting for? Surely Ilse Aigner has long since secured a majority across party lines?" asked SPD parliamentary group leader Matthias Miersch recently. However, Merz, who is friends with Aigner, has remained tight-lipped so far — possibly also because Aigner is not a member of Merz's party, but rather of its smaller sister party, the CSU.
Steinmeier: Christmas makes our lives more hopeful
Several female presidential candidates

Other potential successors from the CDU membership have also been mentioned: Bundestag President Julia Klöckner, former Defense Minister Annegret Kramp-Karrenbauer and Education Minister Karin Prien. Hesse's state premier, Boris Rhein, is also a possible candidate. In recent days, another name has been making the rounds: lawyer Ines Claus, who serves as CDU's parliamentary group leader in Hesse and deputy party chair at the federal level — and is largely unknown.

However, rumors that she would be nominated were swiftly shot down by the chancellor. Sources close to Merz emphasized that he has so far "neither made a decision nor put forward a proposal." There are "a number of suitable" options, sources added.

The president is elected every five years by the Federal Convention, which comprises all 630 members of the Bundestag and an equal number of electors who represent the state parliaments. Among them are also prominent figures from the spheres of culture, science, sports and society. The candidate who receives more than 631 votes goes on to assume office. The governing parties — the CDU/CSU and the SPD — have a combined total of 682 votes, a comfortable majority.

blocks.caption: Bundestag President Julia Klöckner currently has a high-profile positionImage: Christoph Soeder/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Presidential role key amid polarization and crisis

The office of the president is often underestimated as merely a ceremonial role. Yet, as an authority standing above the political parties, this person wields considerable political, legal and moral influence. This is especially true in times of political polarization and international crises. While the president does not govern like a chancellor, he or she represents Germany both at home and abroad.

"From a constitutional perspective, the federal president is enormously important. For example, in a political crisis, he could decide whether it makes more sense to dissolve the Bundestag or to advocate for a minority government," explains political scientist Münch. In addition, he reviews and signs laws proposed by politicians.
What happens next?

The federal chancellor and CDU chairman has an interest in an orderly process, say sources close to the government. The "first milestone" will be the meetings of the CDU Presidium and Executive Board on November 9. Until then, discussions will be held with the state chairpersons of the CDU and the CSU. Sources made it clear that the SPD and the Greens will also be consulted, "since the election of the federal president should have broad support across the democratic spectrum."
That is how political scientist Münch sees it: "I still consider the question open, with a slight edge for CSU candidate Ilse Aigner." But there could still be a real surprise, Münch adds.
This article was originally published in German.

articles.title: Human trafficking victims stranded in Guinea-Bissau
articles.summary: Dozens of West Africans lured to Guinea-Bissau with promises of jobs and migration to Europe say they were exploited by a suspected trafficking network. Now many cannot afford to return home.

image.caption: For years, thousands of young West Africans have migrated to escape conflict, repression and poverty [FILE: 2020]Image: Aline Deschamps/Middle East Images/picture alliance

blocks.text: This article contains descriptions of rape, exploitation and sexual assault. Reader discretion is advised.
Sadio Konimba had hoped for a better future. The 26-year-old had lost her husband and was left alone with her child in Bamako, the capital of Mali.

When an acquaintance told her about the possibility of reaching Europe via the West African nation of Guinea-Bissau, she decided to make the journey. She left her 6-year-old daughter behind with relatives for the time being.
Konimba says she was invited to the country's capital, Bissau, with the promise of work and better chances of eventually continuing on to Europe.

She was told the journey from Bamako to Bissau would cost between 100,000–125,000 CFA francs (roughly €150-€190, or $170-$210), which she paid. She had only intended to stay temporarily in Guinea-Bissau, but when she wanted to return to Mali, her money was not refunded.
"I had to pay a large sum of money," Sadio told DW, adding that instead of the prospects she had been promised, she was confronted with a very different reality.

According to Konimba's account, men from Senegal offered to repay the money she had paid if she "worked" for them. When she realized what that meant, she refused and demanded her money back. To this day, she has received nothing.

Jane, a 21-year-old woman from Sierra Leone, recounted how she was subjected to an attempted rape and other abuses at the hands of a criminal network. She told French news agency Agence France-Presse they even tried to force her into prostitution.

Sadio and Jane are among dozens of victims of a suspected human trafficking ring that was dismantled by police following an operation in Guinea-Bissau on October 21. The intervention followed complaints from victims who had reported abductions and fraud.
In a written statement to DW, the criminal investigation police said that more than five suspects had been arrested.
Trapped by fales promises
According to police, the network used a front company to lure people with promises of jobs and assistance with migration to Europe.

Around 70 people are believed to have fallen victim to the scheme. Most came from abroad, including Guinea, Mali, Cote d'Ivoire and Senegal. The suspected perpetrators allegedly charged victims between 400,000 and 700,000 CFA francs for each journey to Guinea-Bissau.

According to preliminary findings, the victims were held against their will in Bissau, subjected to pressure and forced to take part in fraudulent pyramid schemes. They were expected to recruit additional participants into the schemes through social media.

To make their operations appear legitimate, those responsible allegedly used false contact details for supposed offices in Canada, the United States and Portugal. Information from Interpol, the international police agency, helped investigators uncover the network, according to police.
Scam factories and human trafficking
Issa, a 23-year-old from Guinea, says he paid a smuggler 10 million Guinean francs (around €1,000). When he refused to recruit more people, he was allegedly threatened with death.
A growing criminal network
For Bubacar Ture, head of Guinea-Bissau's Human Rights League, the case is an alarming sign.

"As a human rights organization, we are extremely concerned about this phenomenon, which has now reached deeply troubling proportions," he told DW. In May, authorities rescued 60 foreign nationals during a similar operation.

Ture sees a link between the human trafficking problem and Guinea-Bissau's weak institutions. Criminal networks exploit these conditions to continue their activities, he said, noting that women are particularly vulnerable to human rights abuses.
The small Portuguese-speaking West African country has been plagued by political instability since independence in 1975 and is also known as a transit hub for cocaine bound for Europe.
Rescued, but still trapped far from home
A week after their rescue, the victims face a new problem: many lack the funds needed to travel back to Mali, Sierra Leone or elsewhere in West Africa.

Sadio Konimba is temporarily staying with an acquaintance in Bissau. Her friend told DW that Konimba had been deeply traumatized by what she had experienced. She had never imagined she could fall into the hands of a human trafficking network that might force her into prostitution.
Trapped in the human trafficking network
Konimba herself does not want to discuss in detail what kind of work she was asked to do. Police confirm that women in such cases are often sexually exploited.
Konimba says she has managed to borrow around 75,000 CFA francs from acquaintances in recent days. But that falls short of the cost of her journey back to Bamako.

According to available information, Guinea-Bissau's migration and border authority, the Direcao-Geral de Migracao e Fronteiras (DGMF), also lacks the funds needed to finance the victims' return journeys.
Contacts have been established with the diplomatic missions of the countries concerned. But progress appears slow, and no concrete arrangements for their return have yet been announced.
Support systems falling short
Bubacar Ture criticizes the lack of protection available to victims.

"There are no public shelters for cases like these," he told DW, noting that private facilities have limited capacity, and psychological support and funding for temporary accommodation are also lacking.
The human rights advocate commends the criminal investigation police for taking action against the networks despite limited resources. At the same time, he calls for greater support.
"We make an urgent appeal to the government and international partners to provide adequate support to the judiciary, the police and the other institutions," he told DW.
For Konimba, one thing matters above all else now: returning to Bamako.
"Now I definitely want to go back to my mother and my daughter," she told DW. "Every day she asks me, 'Mom, are you coming home?' I tell her, 'I will come, I will come. Just wait a little longer.'"
But Konimba still does not have enough money for the journey. She is free, but for her, the struggle to rebuild a life with dignity has only just begun.

articles.title: Who will be Bangsamoro's first elected Chief Minister?
articles.summary: Abdulraof Macacua and Ahod Balawag Ebrahim, the present and former interim chief ministers of the Bangsamoro Transition Authority, have emerged as the top contenders for the post as first elected…

blocks.text: Published October 29, 2026 10:15pm

Abdulraof Macacua and Ahod Balawag Ebrahim, the present and former interim chief ministers of the Bangsamoro Transition Authority, have emerged as the top contenders for the post as first elected chief minister when members of the Bangsamoro parliament vote on Friday, October 30.

Both were appointed by the President — Ebrahim by then President Rodrigo Duterte in 2019 and Macacua by President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. in 2025 — and have won seats in the recent BARMM elections for the parliament.
Who will be BARMM's first elected chief minister?
Abdulraof Macacua
According to the Bangsamoro Transition Authority’s website, Macacua was born in the town of Gambar, Maguindanao in 1957. During his youth, Macacua witnessed the Bangsamoro’s struggle for liberation.
He entered the military by 1971, joining the revolutionary movement. He would eventually become the Bangsamoro Islamic Armed Forces’ (BIAF) Chief-of-Staff.

Macacua is considered a key member of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) Peace Negotiating Panel, which eventually paved the way for the passage of the Bangsamoro Organic Law (BOL), which was the foundation of BARMM.
Macacua would become the Secretary General of the United Bangsamoro Justice Party (UBJP), which is the political party of MILF.
Since 2019, Macacua has been a member of the Bangsamoro Transition Authority (BTA), serving as the Minister of the Ministry of Environment, Natural Resources, and Energy.
He was also a member of parliament, as well as a senior minister in the BTA.
In 2023, Macacua was appointed by Marcos as the officer-in-charge of the newly created Maguindanao del Norte province.

Marcos would again appoint Macacua to a different position in 2025, this time as the interim chief of BARMM. He had been expected to serve as the interim chief until the first ever BARMM parliamentary elections.
While Macacua has had a long political career, his position as the interim chief has been challenged by no less than the MILF itself, with the group questioning how Marcos appointed him.
Marcos was supposed to choose a chief based on the list that the MILF provided. However, the MILF said that Marcos chose a chief minister and members of parliament who were not endorsed.
In a separate incident, Macacua was ambushed by armed assailants during a convoy in Maguindanao del Norte in 2026.
Ahod Balawag Ebrahim

Born in Maguindanao in 1949, Ebrahim studied at the Cotabato Public High School in Cotabato City before enrolling at the Mindanao State University-Marawi. He would later transfer to Notre Dame University in Cotabato City, according to the BARMM’s official website.
Ebrahim would eventually join the Moro liberation movement in 1968, quitting his formal education.
The Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF) appointed him as the zone commander after undergoing military training abroad.

By 1974, Ebrahim became the military chairman of the MNLF for the Kutawato Region (present day North Cotabato, Maguindanao, Sultan Kudarat, South Cotabato, and Sarangani). He became the region’s chairman in 1978.

In 1982, the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) was created, where he was appointed as the vice chairman for the Vice Chairman for Military Affairs and the Chief of Staff of the Bangsamoro Islamic Armed Forces (BIAF).
Ebrahim would later become the chair of the MILF Peace Panel negotiating team with the Philippine government from 2001 to 2003. He signed peace agreements on behalf of the MILF.
He would later become the MILF chair after the passing of Shiekh Salamat Hashim in 2003.
During his chairmanship, the Framework Agreement on the Bangsamoro (FAB) and the Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro (CAB) were signed.
When the BOL was passed into law in 2018, Ebrahim was appointed by Duterte as the chief minister of the Bangsamoro Transition Authority (BTA).
He would remain as the interim chief of the BTA until he resigned in 2025 to campaign for the Bangsamoro Parliament election. Ebrahim was replaced by the current interim Chief Minister Macacua.
Ebrahim is currently with the United Bangsamoro Justice Party (UBJP). He remains influential among MILF members and longtime Bangsamoro leaders. —NB, GMA News

articles.title: Shock of rail tragedy gives way to sorrow and outrage in politically divided Spain
articles.summary: The latest train crash will pile pressure on the government of Pedro Sánchez, one month before the general election.

blocks.text: The chaos and horror of Spain's second rail tragedy this year has been conveyed vividly by survivors of Wednesday's high-speed crash that has left at least 69 people dead.

But as Spain holds three days of mourning, revelations from leaked audio recordings of the apparent human error in a control room in the minutes before this disaster happened have given way to public disbelief and outrage, in a highly politicised climate, exactly a month before Spaniards go to the polls.
"You don't know what's happening, you don't know what has happened, you just know that you're being thrown around in a matter of seconds," said Iñaki García, 60.
He was on the stationary Iryo train that was rammed from behind by a Renfe train on the Madrid-Seville line near Urda, around 140km (87 miles) south of the capital.
"There were people injured, walking around, there were dead people," he said. "In the next carriage along there were a lot of dead people."
Recalling the horrific scenes around him, one young man told the BBC in a quivering voice: "I don't know if that's something I'll ever recover from."
Stories of tragedy have continued to emerge. A pharmacist from Urda was one of the first to reach the scene, bringing with him first aid supplies and medicine.
"One of [the passengers] was saying goodbye to his wife and children. His last words were 'God is good'," Antonio García told Spanish radio.
However, the overriding sentiment that these two tragedies have generated is one of confusion and a failure to comprehend how this could have happened.
Not long ago, the speed, efficiency and safety of Spain's high-speed rail system, the largest in Europe, was the envy of its neighbours.
The Adamuz crash triggered a nationwide debate about whether the network was fit for purpose.

This latest incident intensifies pressure on the left-wing government of Pedro Sánchez, in the middle of an election campaign where his Socialist PSOE is behind the conservatives in most opinion polls.
On Wednesday night a demonstration protesting at the government's handling of the rail network saw far-right groups turn out and clash with police.

Although the main parties, other than the far-right Vox, have suspended campaigning, Sánchez has twice visited the scene of the crash and his People's Party rival Alberto Núñez Feijóo came to Urda on Thursday.

Sánchez's transport minister, Óscar Puente, made clear from the start that a computer failure followed by human error was the likely cause of the crash. By late evening, leaked audio recordings of a control-room operator talking to train drivers appeared to back that up.
Puente has long been a hate figure for the right, and with two of the worst rail tragedies in Spanish history taking place on his watch, the criticism is only going to increase.

Spain's biggest train drivers' union Semaf condemned the leak of audio recordings as irresponsible and slanted. The union had already called a strike for Thursday in a bid to ensure that "urgency to travel is never prioritised over safety".

One train driver, Vicente Almenar, told Spanish media: "They always look for the last link in the chain, where it's weakest, but here the entire procedure failed because we don't even know what our colleague was seeing on the screen," he told Spanish media.
Sánchez had not been expecting rail safety to dominate his campaign, but that now looks increasingly likely.

After two accidents and more than 100 deaths on the same high-speed line, Feijóo told reporters in Urda on Thursday: "The Spanish people need answers. They are wondering what is happening to high-speed rail in their country."
And he emphasised that politics was not about talking - it was about acting.

articles.title: Safe access sought for PWDs in cemeteries during Undas
articles.summary: The National Council on Disability Affairs (NCDA) urged local government units (LGU) to ensure that persons with disabilities (PWD) have safe access to cemeteries during the Undas season.

blocks.text: Published October 29, 2026 10:05pm
The National Council on Disability Affairs (NCDA) urged local government units (LGU) to ensure that persons with disabilities (PWD) have safe access to cemeteries during the Undas season.
According to the NCDA, both the Accessibility Law and the Magna Carta for Persons with Disabilities mandated that public places must be kept in proper order and free from obstruction.

“This includes ensuring clear pathways, installing temporary ramps over elevated steps, providing visible signage and adequate lighting, and prohibiting vehicles, merchandise, or any objects from blocking designated access routes,” the NCDA said in a statement.
The group also said that beyond complying with the law, providing reasonable accommodation to PWDs is also an act of respect and equality.

“Every Filipino has the right to honor the memory of their loved ones with dignity. The agency therefore calls on all local government units to conduct inspections and make necessary adjustments before crowds begin flocking to cemeteries,” the NCDA said.
Millions of people are expected to go to cemeteries to visit their dead loved ones this Undas season, with many of them traveling back to their provinces. — BAP, GMA News

articles.title: Erin Patterson prepares for mushroom murders appeal ruling to learn if she could face retrial or longer jail term
articles.summary:
Victorian court to hand down decision on Friday on two appeals regarding Patterson’s triple murder case

  • Get our
articles.byline: Nino Bucci Justice and courts reporter

blocks.text: Erin Patterson is set to find out if she could face a longer prison sentence or a new trial, as Victoria’s highest court hands down its decision on two appeals regarding her triple murder case.
The court of appeal is set to rule on the two appeals from 10am on Friday, after justices Lesley Taylor, Stephen McLeish and Peter Kidd heard arguments from her legal team and prosecutors in August.
Patterson, 52, is not expected to attend the appeal decision in person.

She was last year sentenced to life imprisonment, with a non-parole period of 33 years, for the murders of her estranged husband’s parents, Don and Gail Patterson, and his aunt Heather Wilkinson, after she hosted them for lunch.
Patterson was also convicted of the attempted murder of Heather’s husband, Ian Wilkinson, who survived the beef wellington laced with death cap mushrooms after spending weeks in hospital.
She has appealed against her convictions, while the director of public prosecutions appealed against Patterson’s sentence, arguing that it was manifestly inadequate.
In August, the court heard Patterson should have been given no possibility of ever being released from prison, or a non-parole period so lengthy that she was likely to die behind bars.

Her lawyers argued seven grounds for her appeal, including that allowing jurors to stay in the same hotel as police and the prosecution while they deliberated over their verdicts in the triple murder trial represented a “catastrophic” failure of the justice system.
Richard Edney, for Patterson, said the failure to properly separate the jury during their deliberations was a fundamental irregularity that had denied her a fair trial.
“What we say has occurred here in the applicant’s trial was an inexplicable and perhaps still unexplained failure of a process,” Edney told the court in August.

They also argued that the trial judge Christopher Beale erred in ruling that photos and videos related to mushrooms and found on an SD card in Patterson’s home was inadmissible, as it tended to support her evidence that she foraged for mushrooms.
During the hearings, Brendan Kissane KC, the DPP, said that even though Patterson would be aged in her 80s by the time she was eligible for parole, her sentence was still too lenient.

When asked whether a longer non-parole period would essentially damn Patterson to dying behind bars, and had “some artifice of it being life with life”, Kissane told the court: “It has its harsh aspect to it, of course, we accept that.”
“But in our submission that is not a matter that is outweighed by the seriousness of the offending.”

There are several possible outcomes to Patterson’s appeal: leave to appeal is not granted; leave to appeal is granted, but her appeal dismissed; leave to appeal is granted, her appeal upheld and a retrial ordered; or her leave to appeal is granted, the appeal upheld, and acquittal entered.
If either of the final two decisions are handed down, there will be no need to rule on the DPP’s sentence appeal.
If not, either the appeal fails, or it succeeds and Patterson is resentenced by the court of appeal.

articles.title: Rock collapse kills two in Turkey's Cappadocia, local media reports
articles.summary: One of the region's famous rock formations, known as "fairy chimneys", reportedly collapsed outside an open-air museum.

blocks.text: At least two people have been killed and five injured after a rock formation collapsed at a tourist site in Turkey's historical region of Cappadocia, local media is reporting.
One of the rock spires, which are known as fairy chimneys, reportedly disintegrated at the popular open-air museum in the central town of Göreme.
Nevşehir provincial Governor Hüseyin Kök said the victims' bodies had been recovered from under the rubble, but the justice minister warned there could be "other potential victims" still trapped.
The cause of Thursday's incident was not immediately known, however local media reported the collapse could have been triggered by heavy rain.
Turkish media reported that the collapse happened near the entrance to the museum at about 15:15 local time (12:15 GMT).
In a later post on social media, Justice Minister Akın Gürlek said that "according to initial assessments, two individuals have lost their lives in the incident, and five others have been injured".
He added that a search and rescue operation was continuing at the site.
The Cappadocia region attracts tourists from around the world, who want to see the ancient fairy chimneys - tall, cone-shaped rock formations that are created by volcanic activity.
